About Dutchie

Founded in 2017, Dutchie is a comprehensive technology platform powering dispensary operations, while providing consumers with safe and easy access to cannabis. Dutchie aims to further support the positive societal change the cannabis industry brings to the world through wellness benefits, social justice, and empowering local communities through tax revenue. Powering thousands of dispensaries across 40+ markets throughout the United States and Canada, Dutchie is the leading technology company in the cannabis space and was named in Fast Company’s 10 Most Innovative Companies in North America and listed two years in a row on LinkedIn’s Top 50 Startups.

Dutchie has raised over $600M in funding to date, backed by D1 Capital Partners, Tiger Global, Dragoneer, DFJ Growth, Thrive Capital, Howard Schultz, Snoop Dogg’s Casa Verde Capital, Gron Ventures, members of the founding team at DoorDash, Kevin Durant’s Thirty Five Ventures, and other notable angel investors.

About This Job

As a Marketing Strategy Consultant I on Dutchie's Solutions team, you will be the driving force behind unlocking the full value of Dutchie's Loyalty & Marketing product for our customers.

Loyalty & Marketing is Dutchie's best-in-class solution for helping dispensaries turn one-time shoppers into lifetime customers — combining loyalty program management with integrated SMS, MMS, and email marketing tools, all natively built into the Dutchie platform.

Many dispensaries have already purchased Loyalty & Marketing but have barely scratched the surface of what it can do for their business, and are often leaving significant GMV and messaging revenue (SMS, MMS, email) on the table. Your job is to change that.

You'll use reporting and data tools to proactively identify which customers have the greatest untapped opportunity for growth, then partner closely with Customer Success and Account Management to get in front of those accounts. Once engaged, you'll roll up your sleeves — not just advising on marketing strategy, but hands-on helping customers configure the platform, build campaigns, and set up workflows correctly. You'll review customer data, demographics, market trends, competitive dynamics, and state regulations to help each account launch a marketing strategy that performs, spanning SMS, MMS, and email, and grounded in strong loyalty program fundamentals.

This isn't a "set it and forget it" engagement. You'll stay close to the account through launch, review performance, and iterate on the strategy until adoption, messaging revenue, and retention are clearly trending in the right direction — then hand the customer a playbook and SOPs they can run with going forward. This proactive engagement is also a key lever in reducing churn among underengaged, at-risk accounts. Along the way, you'll be one of our most important sources of voice-of-customer intelligence, feeding real field insight back to our Product team.

What You'll Do…

Opportunity Identification & Prioritization

  • Proactive Account Sourcing: Use reporting tools (Hex or similar BI/data tools) to analyze usage, performance, and GMV data across the Loyalty & Marketing customer base and identify accounts with the greatest opportunity for improved adoption and revenue lift.
  • Prioritization: Continuously triage and rank opportunities so your time — and your Customer Success and Account Management partners' time — is focused on the accounts with the most upside.

Customer Marketing Strategy & Enablement

  • Consultative Diagnosis: Review each account's customer data, demographics, local market trends, competitive landscape, and state-specific regulations to shape a tailored marketing strategy.
  • Campaign Strategy: Advise customers on what campaigns to run, who to target, when to run them, and how to use SMS, MMS, and email effectively together as part of a cohesive strategy.
  • Hands-On Technical Enablement: Go beyond high-level advice — directly help customers configure the platform, build campaigns, and set up workflows correctly so they can execute their strategy without friction.
  • Loyalty Program Optimization: Bring a strong point of view on what makes retail loyalty programs successful, and help customers structure programs that build repeat, lifetime customers.
  • Playbook Development: Build SOPs and marketing playbooks tailored to each customer, so they have a durable, repeatable process to run independently once you hand off.
  • Performance Reviews: Stay engaged with customers post-launch, reviewing campaign and adoption performance and iterating on strategy until results are clearly improving.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • CS & AM Collaboration: Partner closely with Customer Success Managers and Account Managers to coordinate outreach, align on account context, and ensure a seamless customer experience.
  • Product Feedback Loop: Serve as a consistent voice-of-customer channel, surfacing product feedback, feature gaps, and trends from the field to Dutchie's Product team.

What You Bring…

  • 2-4 years of experience in retail marketing, digital marketing, customer marketing, or marketing consulting — B2B SaaS, martech, or customer success experience is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience using a marketing technology platform to manage and run SMS, MMS, and email campaigns — you should be comfortable working directly inside a platform (building campaigns, segmentation, workflows), not just advising from the outside.
  • A solid understanding of data-driven marketing and general marketing optimization best practices — segmentation, targeting, campaign timing/cadence, and performance measurement.
  • Familiarity with retail loyalty programs and what separates a sophisticated, high-performing program from a basic one.
  • Comfort working with data and reporting tools to independently identify trends and prioritize opportunities (e.g., Hex, Looker, Tableau, or similar).
  • Strong consultative instincts — comfortable reviewing a customer's data and market context and translating it into a clear, actionable strategy.

Key Competencies

  • Proactive & Self-Directed: You don't wait to be told which accounts need help — you go find them and bring a plan.
  • Consultative Communicator: Able to build credibility with customers quickly and translate data into a compelling, actionable story.
  • Organized Execution: Comfortable managing multiple customer engagements at once, from initial strategy through performance review and handoff.
  • Cross-Functional Collaborator: Works naturally with Customer Success and Account Management to deliver a coordinated customer experience.
  • Adaptable Marketer: Able to tailor strategy to different markets, regulatory environments, and customer sophistication levels.

Logistics

  • This is a remote, individual-contributor role reporting to the Director, Solutions.
  • Travel: approximately 15%, primarily for customer visits and internal team gatherings.

It's a Bonus if You…

  • Have prior experience running marketing campaigns for cannabis retail operators.
  • Have deeper product/functional experience specifically with Dutchie's Loyalty & Marketing product.
  • Have experience building or scaling SOPs/playbooks for customer-facing teams.

You'll Get…

We are targeting an On-Target Earnings (OTE) of $90,000 - $110,000 (90% base / 10% variable), with variable compensation tied to metrics such as customer adoption of the Loyalty & Marketing product, messaging revenue growth, GMV lift, campaign performance, and customer retention/churn reduction.

In addition to cash compensation, our total rewards package includes:

  • Full medical benefits including dental and vision plans to ensure you always have the best care.
  • Equity packages in the form of stock options to all employees.
  • Technology (hardware, software, reading materials, etc..) allowance
  • Flexible vacation and sick days

Job Title: Technical Release Coordinator

Location: Remote

Position Summary

The Technical Release Coordinator manages and coordinates technology releases across multiple teams and applications. This role owns release schedules, readiness activities, deployment communications, change-management documentation, and post-release reviews.

The Technical Release Coordinator partners with development teams, Scrum teams, infrastructure resources, project leaders, and business stakeholders to ensure releases are properly planned, tested, approved, deployed, and validated. The successful candidate will be highly organized, technically knowledgeable, and comfortable directing off-hours deployment activities while managing risks, dependencies, and competing priorities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate regularly scheduled releases, out-of-cycle deployments, and emergency fixes across multiple teams.
  • Facilitate release-planning meetings to determine scope, sequencing, timelines, dependencies, and deployment requirements.
  • Develop and document release recommendations, including:
    • Release scope and schedule
    • Deliverables and component listings
    • Testing and validation requirements
    • Implementation steps
    • Risk-mitigation and rollback plans
  • Establish release-readiness criteria and track projects through the change-ticket lifecycle.
  • Ensure change tickets are complete and include required testing documentation, implementation instructions, approvals, and rollback plans.
  • Create and maintain the consolidated release calendar, configuration plan, deployment schedule, and stakeholder communications.
  • Prepare for and participate in Change Advisory Board meetings, deployment-planning sessions, and implementation-readiness reviews.
  • Identify scheduling conflicts, missing requirements, technical dependencies, and risks that could affect release outcomes.
  • Direct off-hours release activities, including deployment coordination, status reporting, issue escalation, and resolution.
  • Coordinate mock deployments, pre-production checklists, production implementation, and post-production verification.
  • Compile and review deployment and validation instructions in partnership with development and technical teams.
  • Package and stage production-ready release artifacts.
  • Coordinate the provisioning and readiness of infrastructure resources and environments.
  • Establish and enforce controls for build management, release management, and production change control.
  • Provide input on code-branching and code-merge strategies to project delivery teams and IT stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with technical resources to improve and automate build and deployment processes.
  • Communicate release status, business impact, expected duration, issues, and outcomes before, during, and after deployments.
  • Lead release-review meetings, capture lessons learned, and incorporate improvements into future releases.
  • Maintain release templates, process documentation, procedures, and best practices.
  • Promote continuous improvement across change, build, configuration, and release-management processes.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • More than five years of technology experience, including one to four years of relevant experience coordinating projects or software releases across multiple teams.
  • Experience managing releases of varying size, scope, complexity, and business impact.
  • Knowledge of the software development lifecycle.
  • Experience working with change management processes and production deployments.
  • Hands-on software development experience using object-oriented programming concepts.
  • Experience with code merges, branching strategies, build processes, and deployment activities.
  • General understanding of Agile development practices.
  • General understanding of ITIL practices.
  • Ability to participate in scheduled off-hours, weekend, or emergency release activities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience coordinating releases in a complex enterprise environment.
  • Familiarity with automated build and deployment processes, CI/CD pipelines, and release-management tools.
  • Experience supporting Change Advisory Board processes and IT governance controls.
  • Experience coordinating infrastructure or application-environment provisioning.
  • Knowledge of configuration management, source control, and production validation practices.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong planning, organization, and project-coordination skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple releases, deadlines, and technical dependencies simultaneously.
  • Strong risk-identification, problem-solving, and escalation skills.
  • Ability to communicate technical release information clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate documentation.
  • Ability to influence teams and drive activities to completion without direct authority.
  • Sound judgment when evaluating release readiness, risk, and production impact.
  • Ability to remain composed and make timely decisions during high-impact deployments or production issues.
  • Commitment to process improvement, operational stability, and high-quality release outcomes.

Salary Range: $89,800.00 - $125,500.00

  • Salary is commensurate to experience, location, etc.

Horace Mann was founded in 1945 by two Springfield, Illinois, teachers who saw a need for quality, affordable auto insurance for teachers. Since then, we’ve broadened our mission to helping all educators protect what they have today and prepare for a successful tomorrow. And with our broadened mission has come corporate growth: We serve more than 4,100 school districts nationwide, we’re publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: HMN) and we have more than $12 billion in assets.

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

Serving as a central partner to Site Operations, the Specialist will help ensure that qualifying operational events are converted into complete, factual, and actionable Problem records that strengthen site reliability and reduce the likelihood and impact of recurrence.


Working across Site Operations, the Operations Management Center, Reliability Engineering, Automation Systems, Security, Customer Experience, Legal, vendors, and other technical teams, the Specialist will coordinate root cause analysis tasks, corrective actions, follow on actions and documentation updates while maintaining traceability to the originating incident. A successful candidate will combine strong facilitation, analysis, and operational judgment with the ability to make Problem Management practical for frontline teams. They will maintain high-quality and auditable data, challenge symptom-based conclusions, and translate technical investigations into concise, executive- and customer-ready narratives.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:


· Manage the end-to-end Problem Management lifecycle for qualifying Site Operations incidents, ensuring Problem records are created, assigned, progressed, and closed in accordance with established standards

· Facilitate structured root cause analysis with Site Operations and technical stakeholders, using incident evidence, event timelines, asset history, procedures, and operational data to distinguish root causes from symptoms and contributing factors


· Coordinate corrective and preventive actions across Site Operations, Reliability Engineering, the Operations Management Center, Automation Systems, Security, vendors, and other support teams, with clear owners, target dates, dependencies, and escalation paths


· Maintain accurate, complete, and auditable Problem, problem task, known error, workaround, outage, work order, and related change information in ServiceNow, with traceability to the originating incident


· Support post-incident follow-up for Site Operations P1 and P2 events by validating operational impact, outage details, investigation evidence, and required Problem Management actions


· Analyze recurring incidents, common failure modes, cause codes, and cross-site trends to identify systemic risks and recommend prioritized opportunities for prevention and continual improvement


· Publish and communicate lessons learned, known errors, workarounds, and validated corrective actions so that improvements are adopted consistently across Site Operations and applicable risks are addressed fleet-wide


· Identify and participate in activities focused on process improvement, automation, tools implementation and QA testing


DUTIES:

At DraftKings, AI is becoming an integral part of both our present and future, powering how work gets done today, guiding smarter decisions, and sparking bold ideas. At Acclaro, we're more than a localization company — we're a content intelligence solutions company, and a global team of language enthusiasts, cultural connectors, and technology innovators. Join us on our journey to be the model localization company of the next decade, one that's loved by clients, colleagues, and communities alike.

YOUR NEXT ROLE

As a Localization Project Manager at Acclaro, you'll take ownership of the day-to-day delivery of localization programmes and projects, ensuring work is executed efficiently, accurately, and in line with client expectations. Working closely with Senior Project Managers, Program Managers, and cross-functional teams, you'll coordinate resources, manage schedules, mitigate risks, and drive successful project outcomes across a diverse portfolio of content and services.

THIS ROLE IS FOR YOU IF YOU

YOU’LL STAND OUT IF YOU

Who We Are

At Roadpost, we've spent years building trust with people who need to stay connected beyond cell coverage, in the world's most remote places. That work led to ZOLEO, our global messaging platform powered by the Iridium satellite network, used by adventurers, remote workers, and enterprise teams operating off-grid. The impact is real. Ask the people whose lives were changed by a ZOLEO rescue alert (read their stories).

Today, we're building the next chapter. ZOLEO is evolving from a hardware-led satellite communicator into a safety and preparedness platform, one that combines intelligent monitoring, automation, and real-time visibility to give people and their Safety Circles confidence when it matters most. We're just getting started, and we want people who want to build it with us.

Why This Role Matters

Roadpost is entering the next phase of our NetSuite OneWorld implementation, with a focus on Inventory Management and WMS. Our environment spans 10 subsidiaries and 7 currencies, with integrations including Zone & Co, ZoneCapture/Beanworks, NSPB, and Celigo.

We are looking for a hands-on NetSuite technical expert to provide the internal depth needed to successfully deliver Phase 2, while strengthening our exisiting environment. You will work alongside our implementation partners, independently reviewing technical decisions and delivered work while also helping remediate technical debt remaining from Phase 1.

This is a remote opportunity, and candidates may be located anywhere in Ontario.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead Phase 2 Technical Oversight. Serve as Roadpost’s internal NetSuite expert throughout the Inventory Management/WMS implementation, reviewing solution design, configuration, SuiteScript, SuiteFlow, integrations, and implementation deliverables.
  • Solve Inventory & WMS Challenges. Provide hands-on expertise across serialized inventory, warehouse operations, returns/RMAs, inventory movement, and inventory lifecycle management.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT 321 THE AGENCY321 is a full-funnel creative agency built for brands that operate in complex, regulated industries — healthcare, insurance, legal services, home services, entertainment, and travel and tourism.
jobs.description:
ABOUT 321 THE AGENCY

321 is a full-funnel creative agency built for brands that operate in complex, regulated industries — healthcare, insurance, legal services, home services, entertainment, and travel and tourism. We're a remote, AI-first team that combines strategic creative with CRM infrastructure, performance marketing, and paid media to drive real, measurable business outcomes for our clients.

Technology is central to how 321 competes and grows. From our CRM and automation programs to 321 AIM, our proprietary performance marketing platform, the systems we build are a core part of the value we deliver. The Chief Technology Officer is the executive who sets the vision for that technology and turns it into a lasting competitive advantage.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Chief Technology Officer at 321, you will own the agency's technology vision, strategy, and execution at the executive level. This is a C-suite role with company-wide authority — you'll shape how 321 builds, buys, secures, and monetizes technology, lead the technology organization, and help define the agency's direction as a member of the executive leadership team.

The right person for this role thinks in platforms and business models, not just systems. You understand that the right architecture decisions compound over years, that proprietary technology and data can become defensible products, and that AI is reshaping what an agency can deliver and how it should be priced. You're as comfortable advising on a High Level or Salesforce architecture as you are presenting a multi-year technology strategy to ownership, investors, or enterprise clients — and you build the organization that executes it.

You'll provide executive technology leadership in partnership with 321 AIM, guiding platform architecture, scalability, and roadmap decisions so that our proprietary technology and client service delivery grow together.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Executive Leadership & Technology Vision

  • Define and own the agency's multi-year technology vision and strategy, aligned with company growth goals, service offerings, and market positioning
  • Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, contributing to company strategy, annual planning, and major business decisions
  • Own the technology budget, including platform, licensing, infrastructure, and headcount investments, with clear return-on-investment expectations
  • Lead build-versus-buy-versus-partner decisions for major platforms and capabilities
  • Report on technology performance, risk, and investment outcomes to ownership and, where applicable, investors or a board

Technology Organization & Talent

  • Build, lead, and scale the technology organization, including the Director of Technology and teams spanning CRM/MarTech, integrations, data, AI, and systems administration
  • Design the organizational structure, leadership roles, and hiring plan needed to support the agency's growth
  • Set the culture, engineering standards, and operating principles for how technology is built, shipped, and supported across the agency
  • Develop leaders within the technology organization through coaching, succession planning, and clear career paths

Proprietary Platforms & Product Strategy

  • Provide executive technology leadership for 321 AIM in partnership with its leadership, guiding platform architecture, scalability, reliability, and roadmap priorities
  • Identify opportunities to turn repeatable agency solutions, data assets, and automations into proprietary products, platforms, or productized services
  • Oversee product development practices, including requirements, release management, quality assurance, and technical documentation
  • Protect and grow the agency's technology intellectual property

AI Strategy & Innovation

  • Set the company-wide AI strategy, positioning 321 as a leader in AI-powered marketing, CRM, and performance services
  • Govern responsible AI use, including data privacy, model selection, accuracy standards, and client disclosure practices
  • Lead the evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies that create new service lines, improve margins, or strengthen client outcomes
  • Partner with department leaders to embed AI into creative, paid media, CRM, reporting, and agency operations

Enterprise Architecture, Security & Risk

  • Own the agency's enterprise architecture across internal systems, client platforms, data infrastructure, and integrations
  • Lead the information security program, including policies, access management, vendor risk, incident response, and business continuity
  • Ensure agency and client technology meets regulatory and contractual requirements in healthcare, insurance, legal, and other regulated industries, including HIPAA, business associate agreements, TCPA, GDPR, and CCPA
  • Guide the agency toward formal security and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 as client and growth needs require

Data Strategy & Measurement

  • Define the agency's data strategy, including how client, campaign, and performance data is collected, governed, stored, and used
  • Oversee the measurement and attribution infrastructure that connects marketing activity to closed revenue for clients
  • Build the data foundation needed to support performance-based pricing, benchmarking, and predictive insights across the client portfolio

Client, Partner & Agency Growth

  • Serve as the agency's senior technology executive with clients, partners, and prospects — including CMO, CIO, and ownership-level audiences
  • Lead the technology narrative in new business pitches, RFP responses, and strategic client relationships
  • Build and manage strategic technology partnerships with platforms such as High Level, Salesforce, HubSpot, Google, and Meta
  • Lead technical due diligence for partnerships, acquisitions, or major client engagements as the agency grows

WHAT YOU HAVE

  • 12+ years of experience in technology leadership, with demonstrated depth in MarTech, CRM architecture, data infrastructure, and platform or product development — agency, MarTech, or SaaS experience strongly preferred
  • At least 5 years in an executive or senior technology leadership role (CTO, VP of Technology or Engineering, or Director overseeing multiple teams), including building and scaling technology organizations
  • Proven track record of setting technology strategy and delivering measurable business results, including revenue growth, margin improvement, or new product lines
  • Experience leading the development of proprietary platforms or software products, from architecture and roadmap through launch and scale
  • Deep understanding of CRM and marketing automation ecosystems — High Level strongly preferred; Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, and HubSpot also valued
  • Strong command of enterprise architecture, cloud infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure), APIs, integrations, and data platforms
  • Experience leading security and compliance programs in regulated industries, including HIPAA; SOC 2 or similar framework experience strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated leadership in AI strategy and adoption, including LLM-powered products or workflows, with sound judgment on governance and responsible use
  • Experience owning technology budgets, vendor strategy, and build-versus-buy decisions
  • Executive-level communication skills — able to present technology strategy to ownership, investors, boards, and enterprise clients with clarity and credibility
  • Comfort operating in a fast-growing, remote, multi-client environment with competing priorities
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field — or equivalent demonstrated experience; advanced degree a plus

REPORTING STRUCTURE

The Chief Technology Officer reports directly to the CEO and is a member of the agency's executive leadership team. This role leads the full technology organization, including the Director of Technology and teams spanning CRM/MarTech, integrations, data, AI, and systems administration. The CTO partners with 321 AIM leadership on platform strategy and works closely with the SVP of Strategy, Director of Digital Marketing, Director of Client Strategy, and Creative Director to align technology with client delivery and agency growth.

COMPENSATION

Salary Range: $120K+ annually, based on experience

321 uses a structured compensation framework aligned to role scope, company impact, and agency revenue contribution. Salary placement within range is based on demonstrated executive experience, organizational leadership, and a track record of technology-driven business results. Executive performance bonus eligibility applies.

321 BENEFITS

  • 100% remote work environment
  • Flexible scheduling with core collaboration hours
  • Paid time off + agency-observed holidays
  • Professional development and platform/tool access budget
  • Collaborative, AI-forward team culture that values innovation and continuous learning
  • Opportunity to shape the technology strategy and proprietary platforms of a high-growth agency operating at the intersection of performance marketing and marketing technology
Salary: $120,000+ based on experience

jobs.title: Mentor, Claude Corps (Part-Time)
jobs.excerpt: CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country.
jobs.description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

About the Role

Location: Remote, United States

Role-Type: Part-Time, W2 Employee

Reports To: Senior Manager of AI Practice, Claude Corps

Compensation: $110,000 to $124,500 per year

Start Date: September 21st, ahead of the October 19th cohort launch

Together with Anthropic, CodePath launched Claude Corps in June 2026, a national fellowship program with a $150 million commitment to place 1,000 AI-trained fellows at nonprofits across America. A fellowship is only as good as the engineer riding alongside the fellow when something breaks at midnight. As a CodePath Mentor, that engineer is you.

You are the full-time technical coach for a portfolio of roughly ten pods: about 20 fellows across 8-12 host organizations, from pre-Basecamp through the final day of the program. You are the coach that develops the fellow: you have first eyes on every pull request, you catch the patterns when something is off, and you proactively resolve any roadblocks that come up. The host org directs the fellow's day-to-day work, the curriculum team owns what they learn, and your Sr. Manager of AI Practice is the manager of record who holds the performance bar. Your job is to make each fellow better at the work.

The work is mostly written and asynchronous: code review on pull requests, feedback on roadmap drafts and quarterly business reviews, weekly office hours, and a few synchronous deep dives when something needs more than text. You will not be the deepest expert in the room for every fellow, and we are honest about that. You carry the throughline: you know your pods end to end, see patterns nobody else sees, and pull in deeper expertise the moment a single fellow needs it.

This role is built for engineers who would rather coach 20 engineers through real production work than ship one feature themselves. You are a few years further down the road than the fellows: enough professional reps to read code with judgment, a real coaching instinct, and the AI-native practice fellows are being trained to build.

Key Responsibilities

Coach your pods

  • Carry roughly 10 pods (about 20 fellows across 8 to 12 host organizations) full-time from pre-Basecamp through final day, calibrating your time across the portfolio rather than sinking into one pod

  • Have first eyes on every fellow's pull request, and give structured written feedback on their real work (PRs, roadmap drafts, architecture proposals, QBR deliverables) at the cohort's pace, not your inbox's

  • Facilitate weekly 1:1s with all of the Fellows that report to you and document their progress, challenges, and successes using the tooling that Claude Corps operates on

  • Lead each fellow's Day 30/90/180/270 milestone review; you own the fellow-level synthesis and hand it up to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, who owns the roll-up and the performance call

Deliver the curriculum in your pods

  • Deliver the just-in-time modules the curriculum team designs; author lane- or pod-specific content when they commission it, because you have seen the gap from closer in

  • Frame and debrief the cohort-wide all-hands your Sr. Manager of AI Practice runs, and the sessions where the curriculum team or a guest teaches your fellows directly

  • Co-lead the Basecamp practical assessment alongside Anthropic's instructors; it is your first calibration on each cohort

Keep the program honest

  • When the same problem shows up across three fellows, raise it to the right owner: the Claude Corps leadership team for program efficacy, the curriculum team for curriculum, partner experts for technical depth, host-org managers for a host issue, or your Sr. Manager of AI Practice for a delivery or performance issue

  • Be the first stop when a fellow's technical work is at risk; surface it to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, who owns the escalation

  • Work AI-natively: Claude is core to your coaching loop for code review, pattern-spotting, and feedback at scale, and fellows should see you working the way they are being asked to work

Key Success Metrics

  • You have surfaced the top three cohort-wide technical patterns to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice and the curriculum team

  • 100% of host-org managers you've worked with in the last 30 days can produce one concrete example of your impact

  • Every Day 30 review is done and documented, handed up to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, with a plan for any fellow whose work is at risk or ready for the next challenge

Qualifications

Required

  • 2 to 4 years of professional software engineering on a real team: long enough to have opinions about code, short enough to remember being the most junior engineer in the room

  • Real coaching or mentorship reps, formal or not: an intern you saw through a summer, a teammate you onboarded, a bootcamp you TA'd. We are hiring the instinct, not a management title

  • You can read a pull request you didn't write, in a stack you don't use every day, and give feedback that is specific and useful

  • You have shipped production work with AI-assisted development tools and can describe specifically how your workflow changed; you have to be ahead of the fellows on this curve

  • You are comfortable as a generalist coach: you find the answer or the right person quickly, and you trust partner experts to carry the depth you don't

  • Strong written communication; most of your feedback is asynchronous, read by people who don't speak your stack

  • Comfortable with remote, synchronous obligations across US time zones and about two evenings a month for cohort sessions and milestone reviews

Preferred

  • TA, bootcamp coach, fellowship mentor, or instructor experience in a cohort program, even informally

  • Experience at a small or scrappy organization where engineering meant translating business context into technical decisions

  • Comfort across at least two of: web full-stack, data/AI engineering, ML, infra/devops

Compensation

CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position's level, no matter where you live. For this role, we're hiring for an Individual Contributor level position at an annual salary of $110,000 to $124,500. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a 100% remote position—work from anywhere in the U.S.! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program

  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection

  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)

  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support

  • ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt

  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

Pay range
$110,000—$124,500 USD

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

jobs.description:
Overview

Senior Application Security Engineer

One Identity · Information Security, Attack Surface

Senior individual contributor · India · Reports to the Director of Information Security

Why this role exists

Our products are the access control layer for the companies that buy them. Identity Manager, Active Roles, Safeguard and OneLogin decide who gets into everything else a customer runs. That sets the security bar for our code higher than it sits at most software companies, and it's the reason this role works inside engineering rather than alongside it.

Much of what we build is deployed by customers in their own datacenters. When a defect ships, remediation moves at their upgrade cadence, not ours. That changes where the effort belongs: a design flaw caught in a threat model costs a conversation, and the same flaw caught after release costs a coordinated disclosure and a year of upgrade calls. This role is funded to move security earlier.

We're separating from Quest Software and building an independent security function. The team is lean and globally distributed, and this role is the security voice in the product organization. Scope comes from what you build into the development lifecycle and from what engineering chooses to adopt.

What you'll do

Design it right

  • Threat model the things that matter: authentication and session handling, privilege elevation paths, connector and integration boundaries, tenant isolation in hosted offerings, and cryptographic and secrets handling. You choose where the depth goes.
  • Set security requirements early enough to shape a design instead of contesting one. Engineering teams should meet you at the architecture stage, not at the release gate.
  • Give product and engineering leadership a defensible read on which risks are worth carrying, in language a release decision can be made from.

Work in the code

  • You'll hold commit access to product repositories. A dependency bump, a patched library, a fix in the code path that produced the finding: submit it, review it, and pair with the engineer who owns that module. PRs, not tickets.
  • Own static analysis, dependency scanning, and dynamic testing across the product lines. Tune them until the signal is worth the interruption, and route findings to the team that can act on them.
  • Raise the ceiling on secure coding across a large .NET and Java codebase: patterns, libraries, and reference implementations that make the safe approach the convenient one, plus the review depth to know when they're being used correctly.
  • Take a position on AI-assisted development. Engineering is generating code with it, and someone needs to decide what review that code gets, where automated remediation is trusted to open a pull request, and how we verify what it changed.

Stand behind what ships

  • Own product vulnerability response end to end: intake from researchers and customers, triage across affected versions, coordinated disclosure, CVE handling, and the advisory customers actually read.
  • Turn penetration test and bug bounty findings into fixes and into the systemic change that prevents the next one. Recurrence is the signal that a control is missing, not that a bug was missed.
  • Own software composition analysis and SBOM generation across the product lines, including the license and provenance data Legal and customers depend on.
  • Make product security evidence available on demand. Customer questionnaires, security reviews, and certification work all draw on the same underlying facts, and they should be produced from one source.

What we're looking for

Required

Six or more years in software engineering or security, with at least three focused on application or product security. Equivalent depth counts.

  • Application security experience on a product that customers deploy and operate themselves, with the release and disclosure realities that come with it.
  • Code-level fluency in C# and .NET, and enough range to be useful in a Java codebase. You read and write production code, not just findings.
  • Hands-on work with AI-assisted development or AI-enabled security tooling within the last six months, and a considered view on where it belongs in a review pipeline.

The three above are the bar. Everything below is depth we'd like and can build. If you meet the requirements and bring most of the rest, apply. We'd rather assess the gap ourselves than have you decide it for us.

Also matters: threat modeling at design time with engineering in the room; static, dynamic and composition analysis tooling and the judgment to tune it; identity and authentication protocols including OAuth, OIDC, SAML and SCIM; coordinated vulnerability disclosure and CVE handling; secure code review depth in web and API surfaces; the ability to hold a position with senior engineers and change it when they're right.

Helpful: SBOM standards and license compliance, cryptographic review, security champions programs, PCI DSS or FedRAMP applied to a product rather than a company, prior time as a product engineer.

What you should know going in

This role is embedded in engineering by design, with the access to prove it. You'll work across every product line, which means breadth before depth and a constant judgment call about where your attention is worth most. The work is visible to engineering leadership and it reaches customers directly through what ships and what we're able to tell them. If you want to be measured by what got fixed rather than what got filed, this is that seat.

Company Description

One Identity enables organizations of all sizes to better secure, manage, monitor, protect, and analyse information and infrastructure to help fuel innovation and drive their businesses forward.

With team members around the globe, we intend to continue to grow revenues and add value to customers.

When you join our team, you will have the opportunity to build and develop products at a scale few others can provide.

Our product portfolio serves a large base of customers and we are addressing the strategic imperatives for enterprise businesses.

Why work with us?

Life at One Identity means collaborating with dedicated professionals with a passion for technology.

When we see something that could be improved, we get to work inventing the solution.

Our people demonstrate our winning culture through positive and meaningful relationships.

jobs.excerpt: About the role:As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical.
jobs.description:
About the role:

As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly.

Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years.

We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions.

We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace.

How this role fits alongside our other AI roles: this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data & AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI.
  • Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards.
  • Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance.
  • Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements.
  • Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope.
  • Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors.
  • Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury.
  • Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates.

Core responsibilities:

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations.
  • Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact.
  • Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies.
  • Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app platform, agent orchestration frameworks, and the data access and governance layer.
  • Establish and refine AI-specific compliance standards for the department—what evidence a launch requires, what must be logged, what requires human review, what must be escalated, and what is out of bounds—and ensure those standards evolve as the organization and the technology grow.
  • Support new product launches and expansions by scoping, defining, and communicating compliance requirements clearly and early, including for co-marketing and distribution partnerships with third-party AI platforms.
  • Monitor regulatory, supervisory, and industry developments relevant to AI in financial services, assess impact, and drive implementation of required changes.
  • Own and oversee multiple concurrent high-impact AI compliance workstreams, holding project owners accountable for results and ensuring each aligns with department and company objectives.
  • Support remediation efforts for products within scope, including root cause analysis, corrective action planning, and execution tracking.
  • Partner with executive leadership, partner bank compliance teams, and external advisors to guide high-level decisions on AI direction, presenting data-driven recommendations.
  • Contribute to the broader Compliance function by supporting policy development, documentation standards, audit preparation, and examiner interactions.
  • Help build and reinforce a strong culture of compliance across Mercury through collaboration, education, and influence—including raising the AI fluency of the Compliance team itself, and developing scalable tools, templates, and frameworks others can reuse.

You should have:

  • 8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory, product compliance, or regulatory risk role, ideally within fintech or financial services, with a track record of being the recognized authority in your domain.
  • Demonstrated experience advising on AI, machine learning, or model-driven products in a regulated environment—or comparable experience standing up a new compliance domain where no playbook existed.
  • Working knowledge of the regulatory and supervisory framework relevant to AI in banking, including UDAAP, fair lending and ECOA/Reg B, FCRA and adverse action, Reg E and payments authorization, BSA/AML, GLBA and privacy, marketing and disclosure requirements, recordkeeping, complaint management, model risk management expectations, and third-party and vendor risk management guidance.
  • Familiarity with emerging AI-specific regimes and frameworks and the ability to form a practical view on their application—such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, state AI and automated decisioning laws.
  • Technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on model behavior, evaluation and testing, agent permissioning and tool scoping, logging and observability, and data access controls—and to know which questions actually surface risk.
  • Deep experience partnering with product and engineering teams on regulatory and compliance matters across the product lifecycle, including on fast-moving launches with external dependencies.
  • Proven ability to own highly ambiguous, large-scale compliance problems and to create and execute a strategy to address them, without waiting for precedent.
  • Experience designing compliance frameworks that span multiple product lines or departments, and improving systems and processes so that compliance posture evolves alongside business growth.
  • Demonstrated success operating with senior stakeholders, including executives, partner banks, auditors, or regulators, and presenting data-driven recommendations that drive decisions.
  • Strong project management skills, including the ability to define problems, create execution plans, manage several high-impact initiatives at once, and drive outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate regulatory and financial partner risk into terms stakeholder teams understand, and to resolve conflict around risk tolerance, resourcing, and timelines.
  • Experience mentoring mid-level compliance professionals and raising the capability of a team, not just delivering your own work.
  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with sound judgment on when to move and when to escalate.
  • Curiosity, adaptability, and genuine interest in engaging with frontier technology and the regulatory challenges that come with it.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

Total Rewards

jobs.excerpt: Who We ArePindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:

Is this identity synthetic? Detect AI-generated and manipulated voice and video.
Is this identity risky? Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.
Is this identity known? Authenticate identities using voice, device, behavioral, and other signals.

Pindrop brings this intelligence together across purpose-built trust engines to help organizations make informed decisions in real time — protecting customers, workforce interactions, and emerging AI-driven interactions.

Pindrop protects billions of high-risk interactions for enterprises, including leading financial institutions, insurers, and healthcare organizations. Its technology is informed by more than 8 billion real-world interactions annually and protected by 300+ patents.

Recognized by TIME as one of the 10 Most Influential Software Companies of 2026 and by Inc. for Best in Business for Innovation, Pindrop is backed by leading investors including Andreessen Horowitz, IVP, and CapitalG.

As a Staff Software Engineer on the Authentication team, you will set technical direction for the cloud services and infrastructure behind Passport, guiding the team through its continued migration to the cloud platform. You will operate beyond a single service or sprint, leading complex, multi-quarter initiatives that improve the reliability, scalability, performance, and security posture of Authentication's systems.

This is an individual contributor role with broad technical influence and no direct people-management responsibility. You will partner closely with engineering leaders, product, test and research to shape architecture, resolve systemic risks, and turn ambiguous problems into durable solutions. More specifically, you will:

  • Define and evolve the technical strategy and architectural direction for Passport's cloud services, spanning multiple subsystems and workflows.
  • Lead high-impact, ambiguous initiatives from problem framing and design through implementation, rollout, and operational follow-through, using Go and Python.
  • Set technical standards and reusable patterns for cloud-native services across AWS and GCP, including services such as Kinesis, DynamoDB, and S3, with a focus on reliability, scale, and secure production operation.
  • Make and communicate consequential tradeoffs involving reliability, scalability, latency, security, cost, and time to market.
  • Anticipate systemic risks, identify architectural gaps, and drive mitigation before they affect customers, delivery velocity, or operational stability.
  • Partner closely with software engineering, test engineering, research, product teams to align roadmaps and deliver new capabilities.
  • Lead technical reviews and facilitate alignment on complex design decisions, migration strategies, and ownership boundaries.
  • Participate in incident response for critical systems, translating operational learnings into durable improvements in alerting, runbooks, deployment quality, and service ownership, using modern observability tooling to reduce ticket volume.
  • Raise the effectiveness of engineers across the team through mentorship, code reviews, technical guidance, and hands-on collaboration.
  • Participate in the team's on-call rotation, including helping cover after-hours alerts as the team expands distributed support coverage.

Who you are

  • You are a systems thinker who can connect architectural decisions to customer impact, business priorities, and long-term engineering health.
  • You are an owner who can independently drive work from design through production with strong judgment around performance, scale, and security.
  • You are widely trusted to lead complex technical discussions, create alignment, and influence decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, making progress with incomplete information, and adapting technical direction as new evidence emerges.
  • You communicate complex system behavior, tradeoffs, risks, and decisions clearly to engineers, product, and cross-functional partners.
  • You remain calm and accountable during incidents, architectural challenges, and shifting priorities.
  • You are invested in helping others grow and bring a mentorship mindset to code reviews, collaboration, and team development.
  • You are motivated by authentication, identity, and security-sensitive backend engineering at scale.

Your skill-set

Must-haves:

  • 8+ years of professional software development experience building backend services and APIs, or equivalent practical depth.
  • Demonstrated Staff-level impact: leading significant technical initiatives across multiple services or domains and delivering measurable outcomes.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Go, Python, or similar languages, plus a deep foundation in data structures, algorithms, concurrency, and Linux-based development.
  • Deep experience designing and operating cloud-native systems in AWS or GCP, including managed services such as S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, and IAM.
  • Proven ownership of highly available systems, including deployment, monitoring, troubleshooting, incident response, and operational improvement, using CI/CD, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • Experience defining or influencing technical standards, architecture, or roadmaps across team boundaries.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document decisions and build alignment among stakeholders with different priorities.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with backend data stores and messaging technologies such as Redis, MySQL, RabbitMQ, and Elasticsearch.
  • Experience in authentication, identity, fraud prevention, or other security-sensitive product environments.
  • Strong observability practices across metrics, logs, and traces, with a track record of using them to drive production diagnostics.
  • Experience leading large-scale migrations, reliability programs, or cost and capacity optimization efforts.
  • Experience designing internal platforms, developer tooling, or reusable engineering patterns adopted by multiple teams.
  • Exposure to UI work or adjacent product experiences that connect backend systems to customer-facing workflows.

What’s in it for you

At Pindrop, you’ll work on the backend and platform systems that power Passport, helping secure critical customer interactions where trust, fraud prevention, and identity verification matter every day.

You’ll tackle meaningful cloud engineering challenges that shape reliability, scalability, and the speed at which products reach customers, with direct visibility into the impact of your work. As a staff engineer, you’ll have the opportunity to influence architecture, raise technical standards, and help strengthen a growing team alongside experienced partners across the platform.

You’ll join a company operating at the intersection of authentication, fraud prevention, and deepfake defense, where strong engineering directly supports the business and the customers who rely on it.

What we offer

As a part of Pindrop, you’ll have a direct impact on our growing list of products and the future of security in the voice-driven economy. We hire great people and take care of them. Here’s a snapshot of the benefits we offer:

  • Competitive compensation package, including RSUs (Restricted Stock Units) for all employees, so everyone shares in our long-term success.
  • Remote-first environment - giving you flexibility and autonomy in how you structure your day.
  • While we work flexibly, we prioritize meaningful in-person moments through regular team on-sites, company-wide events, and intentional gatherings that foster connection, collaboration, and shared success.
  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Generous health and welfare plans to choose from - including one employer-paid “employee-only” plan!
  • Best-in-class Health Savings Account (HSA) employer contribution
  • Low-cost vision and dental plans for you and your family, providing comprehensive coverage and peace of mind.

    • One year of diaper delivery for your newest addition to the family! It’s our way of welcoming new Pindroplets to the family!

  • Annual Learning & Development stipend to support your professional growth, skill-building, certifications, and continued education.

We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

AI - A Transformative Force

At Pindrop, we view artificial intelligence as a transformative force that, when harnessed responsibly, can unlock unprecedented value for our customers, partners and society and enable and empower us to continue to deliver cutting-edge technology to combat fraud and unblur the lines between what it means to be human versus machine.
