jobs.title: Legal & Compliance Manager
jobs.excerpt: Wholesale Commercial Insurance Broker;National – Digital First Platform – Real Time Rate, Quote & Bind Compliance at iBynd + SEMSEE has outgrown a shared responsibility.
jobs.description:
Wholesale Commercial Insurance Broker;

National – Digital First Platform – Real Time Rate, Quote & Bind

Compliance at iBynd + SEMSEE has outgrown a shared responsibility. This is a full-time ownership seat. The Compliance Manager will inherit a functioning compliance program across multiple entities and a real book of carrier and vendor relationships, and will be responsible for taking both to the next level: tightening the program and putting the foundation in place for the next stage of growth. This is an individual contributor role reporting directly to the COO, working in close partnership with Finance and Accounting.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

COMPLIANCE PROGRAM OVERSIGHT

  • Take full ownership of the existing compliance program and mature it across both iBynd and SEMSEE entities — written policies and procedures, training, monitoring, internal audit, producer oversight, anti-fraud and AML obligations, and the compliance committee cadence.
  • Identify compliance gaps, prioritize them by risk, and close them. Define what 'good' looks like for this company at the next stage of scale and put the controls in place to get there.
  • Oversee state regulatory and licensing across all operating states — entity licenses, producer/P&C licenses, and surplus lines broker licenses — ensuring the company's full licensing footprint is current, accurate, and audit-ready.
  • Provide tax compliance guidance in partnership with accounting, ensuring state-by-state obligations, surplus lines tax filings, and applicable programs are properly maintained and overseen.
  • Partner with Accounting and Finance on premium trust and fiduciary account compliance — segregation of premium funds, agency-bill and direct-bill reconciliation, carrier bordereaux and producer commission accounting, and support for financial statement, carrier, and regulatory audits.
  • Work with outside tax advisors on the entity-level obligations that follow the licensing footprint — state registrations and nexus, apportionment, franchise and gross receipts filings, and 1099/1042 information reporting for producers and vendors.

CONTRACTING & CARRIER RELATIONSHIPS

  • Support our Carrier appointments, binding authority and program agreements, reinsurance treaties where applicable, MGA arrangements, and the full stack of vendor, partner, and technology contracts.
  • Serve as the primary initial point of contact for carrier counterparties, MGA/MGU partners, and third-party vendors on all contractual and relationship matters.

DIGITAL PRODUCT & PRIVACY LEGAL SUPPORT

  • Work closely with the COO on legal review of the company's digital platform with particular emphasis on privacy obligations, AI/ML governance in underwriting, and data handling practices.
  • Own the company's privacy compliance program under GLBA and applicable state privacy laws, ensuring policies, notices, and data practices are current and enforceable.
  • Partner with the technology and product teams to build legal and compliance requirements into new platform features and data initiatives from the outset.

QUALIFICATIONS

REQUIRED

• 6–8 years of compliance experience

  • Direct insurance industry experience is required — insurtech, MGA/MGU, wholesale broker, or carrier. Insurtech or digital-first distribution experience is strongly preferred — we want someone who has done this work where the platform, not the paper file, is the system of record. This is not a role for a generalist looking to learn the industry on the job.
  • Working knowledge of accounting as it applies to insurance distribution — premium trust and fiduciary accounting, commission, and the ability to read a general ledger, a reconciliation, and a carrier statement without needing them translated. An accounting degree, CPA, or time spent inside a finance function is a strong plus.
  • Hands-on surplus lines premium tax experience — multi-state filings, and the mechanics of calculating and remitting tax and fees, rather than only supervising someone who does.
  • Working knowledge of surplus lines regulation, producer licensing, and the wholesale distribution model; experience with MGA, MGU, or program business strongly preferred.
  • Experience operating a compliance program — as the owner, a key contributor, or the person who inherited and matured one.
  • Comfort in a technology-forward environment — conversant with how software, data, and AI factor into modern insurance operations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills across a wide range of audiences including regulators, carriers, underwriters, and engineers.

PREFERRED

  • Experience operating or maturing a privacy program under GLBA and modern state privacy laws.
  • CPA or Accounting Background or a professional designation such as CPCU, AINS, CIPP/US, or CAMS.
  • Familiarity with NIPR and Sircon for licensing administration, and OPTins for premium tax remittance.
  • Experience supporting a company through a state market conduct exam, a carrier audit, or a financial statement audit.
Fully Remote Role

At iBynd Semsee, we are committed to upholding the highest standards of employment practices in each jurisdiction we operate in. We ensure that all employees are fairly compensated for their work, in accordance with the provisions outlined by the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

iBynd Semsee is an equal opportunity employer, committed to a diverse workforce. iBynd Semsee complies with federal and state law governing non-discrimination in employment practices.

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION:Public Rights Project (PRP) is a national nonprofit organization that helps local government officials fight for civil rights.
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION:

Public Rights Project (PRP) is a national nonprofit organization that helps local government officials fight for civil rights. We build their capacity to protect and advance civil rights, convene and connect them on key issues, and provide legal representation to help them win in court for residents. Since its founding in 2017, PRP has recovered significant financial relief for marginalized people; built a nationwide network of government offices, elected officials, and community-based organizations; trained prosecutors and government lawyers across the country; and secured court victories on rights for abortion, immigrants, workers, and voting. Learn more about our work.

JOB SUMMARY

Public Rights Project seeks to hire two fellows for a one-year fellowship, beginning September 2027. The fellowship is intended for recent law school graduates and lawyers with fewer than three (3) years’ experience, including graduating 3Ls, judicial law clerks, and candidates completing another legal fellowship.

We are looking for candidates with a belief in the power of state and local government to make positive change in the world and a passionate commitment to economic, racial, gender, and environmental justice. A fellowship at Public Rights Project would be ideal for candidates interested in cutting-edge impact litigation, public service, and creative strategies to advance civil rights, combat federal or state abuses of power, and more. The fellow will have an opportunity to work directly with the Managing Attorney, Litigation Director, Civil Rights Hub Director, Election Protection Hub Director, Staff Attorneys, other Legal Fellows, multiple cities and states across the country, and community and nonprofit partners. The fellow will also have an opportunity to contribute to case generation, development, and strategy; draft comments and amicus briefs; support trainings and technical assistance to local governments; and gain valuable experience in organizational and program design.

The prospective fellow is encouraged to apply for any available external funding sources. PRP will guarantee a designated salary and benefits package, regardless of the external funding amount, and will also work to identify independent sources of funding for the fellowship.

We welcome applicants from all jurisdictions. The position will be based remotely, although some travel may be required.

The application window for this Legal Fellow position will close on Friday, October 23, 2026, at 5:00pm ET.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Work on all facets of federal and state court litigation, taking ownership of substantive assignments with guidance from supervising attorneys;
  • Conduct factual and legal research and provide guidance and analysis of laws across a range of jurisdictions;
  • Draft, review, edit analytic and persuasive written work product;
  • Participate in advising government clients, including legal, political, and justice considerations of each particular circumstance;
  • Meet with government and non-government stakeholders;
  • Support and potentially lead legal organizing and outreach efforts;
  • Help oversee and coordinate the summer law clerk program;
  • Synthesize input and feedback from internal and external stakeholders; and
  • Contribute to an innovative, inclusive, and supportive group of advocates.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • J.D. from a U.S. law school (by Spring 2027);
  • Licensed to practice law or applying for a license to practice law in a jurisdiction of the United States; and
  • Experience through a judicial clerkship, legal fellowship, clinic, or other litigation-related work.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Excellent research, analysis, and writing skills, including sound reasoning and persuasive written work;
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in case records, supporting evidence, and legal citations;
  • Familiarity with legal research databases, such as Westlaw or LexisNexis;
  • Eagerness to learn, incorporate feedback, and collaborate with colleagues and clients;
  • Passion for social justice and public service lawyering;
  • Curiosity about the role of government to promote social change;
  • Ability to work well with others and diverse groups;
  • Self-motivation and the ability to structure time effectively; and
  • Experience working with underserved communities in and out of the legal context.

APPLICATION MATERIALS

A resume, cover letter, and law school transcript are required to submit an application. An unofficial transcript is acceptable. The application window for this Legal Fellow position will close on Friday, October 23, 2026, at 5:00pm ET.

ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIP

The Legal Fellow will report directly to the Managing Attorney within the litigation team and will have an opportunity to work with other PRP attorneys, multiple cities and states across the country, and community and nonprofit partners.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Requires sitting, talking, listening, reading, and writing for up to 8 hours per day. Certain situations may require lifting items up to 20 pounds.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Fully remote organization and team. This role may require travel a few times a year to PRP events or meetings. We currently have remote staff in Oakland, Los Angeles, Boston, Philadelphia, Portland (Oregon), and Washington, DC, as well as other cities.

COMPENSATION

The determined salary range for this role is set at $75,000 (for internal equity, PRP can not engage in salary negotiations outside of this range).

PRP HIRING COMMITMENT

PRP is committed to the principles and practices of equal employment opportunity. A diverse and inclusive workplace, both at PRP and within the government offices we serve, is a key ingredient for achieving our mission of building equitable enforcement capacity within state and local government.

We aim to assemble a team that reflects the world we live in and the communities we serve with respect to race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, and immigration status. People with personal or family experience with the type of harms we seek to combat, including wage theft, predatory lending, fraud, discrimination, and environmental degradation are particularly encouraged to apply.

VIDIZMO is an AI software company, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Tysons, Virginia. Over 100 organizations deploy VIDIZMO across public safety, government, healthcare, financial services, education, legal, manufacturing and energy. VIDIZMO is an NVIDIA Inception partner, a Microsoft Solutions Partner for Data & AI, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified.

  • Run product demos on time and log every demo on the deal in HubSpot.
  • Answer technical questions from customers and partners within one working day.

  • Lead the development of the patient promotional platform, including messaging, creative campaigns, and promotional tactics

  • Represent Celcuity as a trusted partner in the oncology community

Qualifications

Required:

`

  • B.S./B.A. in science, business, marketing, or a related field
  • 10+ years of commercial experience in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry
  • 5+ years of oncology marketing experience, including direct patient marketing
  • Proven track record in leading the development and implementation of successful marketing campaigns
  • Product launch experience as a promotional marketer

The Phase 3 VIKTORIA-2 trial is evaluating gedatolisib in combination with palbociclib and either fulvestrant or letrozole for the first-line treatment of HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer. Analytics Engine North Star & Strategy

  • Define and own the North Star for Health Services Analytics as a distinct operating engine, articulating the future-state vision: what the analytics function must become, the capabilities it must build, and the proving metrics that demonstrate it is getting there.

    • Deliver the Unified KPI & Operating Performance Dashboard as the single source of truth for Health Services Operations, rolling into the enterprise Operating Performance Dashboard.
    Standardized Transformation Layer & Data Modernization
    • Build and own the standardized, governed transformation layer between enterprise data products and Health Services analytics products — encompassing metric definitions, transformation pipelines, business logic, enrichment layers, and quality checks — to eliminate duplicated pipelines, inconsistent outputs, and shadow data engineering.
    • In partnership with the Chief Data Officer, lead the migration of Health Services analytical functions from legacy platforms to modern cloud-based solutions, ensuring data arrives at the point of use ready to be consumed without requiring secondary engineering.

    • Shift the analytics engine's work mix from predominantly recurring reporting and ad hoc requests toward advanced analytics, predictive models, AI-enabled workflows, and proactive intelligence — and track that shift as a proving metric of the analytics engine's own maturity.

jobs.description:
Über uns

Ohne Speicher keine Energiewende.

ju:niz Energy entwickelt und betreibt seit über zehn Jahren netzdienliche Großbatteriespeicher. Unsere Anlagen stabilisieren das Stromnetz und schaffen die Flexibilität, die eine Energieversorgung mit erneuerbaren Energien braucht. Wir investieren selbst in unsere Projekte und behalten die Speicher langfristig im Bestand.

Für unser Operations-Team suchen wir dich als Servicetechniker (m/w/d). Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Anlagen sicher und zuverlässig laufen. Du kannst überall in Deutschland wohnen: Von deinem Wohnort aus betreust du unsere Anlagen im gesamten Bundesgebiet. Je nach Einsatzplanung gehören auch mehrtägige Touren mit Übernachtung dazu. Aufgaben, die keine Anwesenheit an der Anlage erfordern, kannst du von zu Hause erledigen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • An unseren Großbatteriespeichern und elektrotechnischen Nebenanlagen führst du Wartungen, Inspektionen und Instandsetzungen durch.
  • Tritt eine Störung auf, grenzt du die Ursache systematisch ein, behebst den Fehler und tauschst bei Bedarf Komponenten aus – vor Ort oder, soweit möglich, per Fernzugriff.
  • Mithilfe von SCADA-, EMS- und Fernwirksystemen überwachst und parametrierst du unsere Anlagen.
  • Bei Inbetriebnahmen, Funktionstests, Netztests und Upgrades bringst du deine technische Erfahrung ein und führst Prüfungen im Rahmen deiner Qualifikation durch.
  • Deine Einsätze, Messergebnisse und Lösungen hältst du nachvollziehbar fest. Wiederkehrende Fehler und Verbesserungspotenziale besprichst du mit dem Operations-Team, damit unsere Anlagen langfristig zuverlässig laufen.

Dein Profil

  • Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung im elektrotechnischen Bereich bildet deine Grundlage – zum Beispiel als Elektroniker für Betriebstechnik, Elektroniker für Automatisierungstechnik oder Mechatroniker mit elektrotechnischer Erfahrung.
  • In der Wartung oder Instandhaltung elektrischer Anlagen, industrieller Steuerungen oder Energieanlagen hast du bereits praktische Erfahrung gesammelt. Kenntnisse von Batteriespeichern sind willkommen, aber keine Voraussetzung.
  • Schaltpläne und technische Dokumentation liest du sicher; bei der Fehlersuche gehst du strukturiert vor.
  • Erfahrung mit EMSR-Technik, SCADA, EMS oder Kommunikationsprotokollen wie Modbus und IEC 61850 ist ein Plus.
  • Eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten liegt dir. Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und besitzt einen Führerschein der Klasse B.
  • Für Einsätze an unseren Anlagen reist du innerhalb Deutschlands. Auch mehrtägige Touren mit Übernachtung sind für dich grundsätzlich möglich.

Warum wir?

  • Technik mit Wirkung: Deine Arbeit trägt dazu bei, dass Großbatteriespeicher zuverlässig funktionieren und das Stromnetz stabilisieren.
  • Abwechslungsreiche Einsätze: Dich erwarten unterschiedliche Anlagen und Aufgaben – von der Fehleranalyse bis zur Inbetriebnahme.
  • Deutschlandweiter Einstieg: Dein Wohnort muss nicht in der Nähe unseres Büros in Aschheim liegen.
  • Fachliche Entwicklung: Bei uns kannst du dein Wissen in der Batterietechnik und im Anlagenbetrieb weiter ausbauen.
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest mit einem kollegialen Team und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

Kontakt

Bewirb dich jetzt – auch wenn dein Lebenslauf nicht alle Punkte erfüllt. Entscheidend sind Motivation, Potenzial und dein Wille, die Energiewende aktiv mitzugestalten.

Wir freuen uns ausdrücklich über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, Perspektiven und Erfahrungen. Gemeinsam schaffen wir ein Umfeld, in dem jeder sein volles Potenzial entfalten kann.

Dein Ansprechpartner

Moritz Erlbeck

People Growth & Hiring Lead

jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY

Serves as the vital bridge between internal operations and our clients, ensuring strict compliance with complex client parameters while safeguarding quality standards. By proactively analyzing audit trends and leading calibration efforts, this role mitigates operational risk, optimizes outcomes, and drives continuous process improvements, including targeted machine learning integration. Ultimately, the position elevates client trust, strengthens internal team capability, and protects organizational revenue through consistent, high-accuracy service delivery.

Mission, Culture & Values

At Dane Street, we believe exceptional employee experiences create exceptional client experiences. Our culture is built on collaboration, continuous improvement, accountability, and care.

We care for our customers, we care for our employees, and we care for one another. Every team member plays an important role in creating an environment where people feel respected, supported, empowered to grow, and inspired to do meaningful work.

What You’ll Do

Quality Calibration and Client Alignment

  • Partner directly with client auditors through monthly review calls and calibration sessions to maintain operational alignment, clarify expectations, and minimize scoring variance.
  • Manage a monthly case sample selection from reconciliation reports using audit criteria, logging scores and deduction points in the designated client portal.
  • Lead the end-to-end audit rebuttal process, investigating findings and presenting timely, data-backed appeals to the client.
  • Maintain, analyze, and upload quality metrics and audit insights within the client portal to ensure real-time visibility into compliance trends and team performance.
  • Lead in-person client touchpoints and strategic business reviews to strengthen trust, align on evolving compliance standards, and reinforce partner satisfaction.

Team Coaching and Continuous Improvement

  • Facilitate regular coaching sessions with the internal QA team to communicate updated client specifications, scoring parameters, and quality standards.
  • Analyze audit trends alongside internal leadership to identify root causes of quality gaps and recommend actionable process solutions.
  • Oversee post-audit action plans, tracking and driving the implementation of process updates and machine learning (ML) enhancements to measurably improve audit performance.

Process Improvement

  • Collaborate with Machine Learning, the client, and operational teams to translate findings and client feedback into actionable automation rules, driving continuous model accuracy and operational efficiency.
  • Validate new machine learning automations and tool features against live sample data before full rollout to ensure they meet client quality benchmarks.
  • Establish and conduct internal calibration sessions across the QA team to ensure baseline consistency and eliminate scoring variances before reports are client-facing.
  • Document new audit methodologies, case guidelines, and client-specific business rules into standardized operating procedures (SOPs) for onboarding and retraining.
  • Design Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) protocols for recurring high-severity errors or systematic compliance failures.

What Makes This Role Successful:

You’re someone who naturally looks for ways to make things better. You bring a thoughtful, detail-oriented approach to reviewing client cases, with the ability to spot both individual issues and larger patterns or opportunities for improvement.

You’re comfortable asking questions, digging into the “why” behind an issue, and using good judgment to determine what needs to change. You communicate your findings clearly and turn them into practical recommendations that the QA team can use to improve workflows.

You take ownership of your work, collaborate well with others, and are motivated by seeing your insights lead to real improvements in quality, consistency, and the client experience. Most importantly, you don’t just identify what isn’t working—you help find a better way forward.

Requirements

What Your First 90 Days May Look Like:

First 30 Days — Transition, Assess & Establish Baseline

Focus on gaining a comprehensive understanding of the Sedgwick audit lifecycle, mastering monthly case selection criteria, scoring reconciliation methods, rebuttal workflows, and client calibration activities.

Approach the onboarding process through a continuous improvement lens. Using a fresh perspective, conduct a deep dive into recent audit outputs and variance trends as you’re learning to establish a performance baseline, pinpoint root causes for scoring deductions, and surface immediate opportunities for process refinement. As an internal auditor, your insights are critical from day one. You are expected and encouraged to speak up, challenge existing workflows, and highlight areas where we can optimize quality and efficiency.

Days 31–60 — Analyze, Improve & Implement

Transition to full operational ownership of the audit and calibration cycle while pivoting insights into tangible process improvements. Partner closely with PAS leadership and the QA team to dismantle recurring quality bottlenecks through root-cause analysis, tighter internal calibration, and direct coaching interventions. Concurrently, serve as the bridge to technology partners, identifying and championing high-value workflow adjustments and machine-learning enhancements that scale overall efficiency and audit accuracy.

Days 61–90 — Optimize, Measure & Sustain

Shift focus toward measuring business impact and institutionalizing continuous improvement. Validate recent process changes and coaching initiatives by measuring shifts in scoring variance and defect trends. Formalize a repeatable, long-term framework for internal calibration, ongoing QA education, and workflow refinement. Finally, establish a regular reporting cadence for executive leadership, delivering transparent visibility into risk areas, implemented solutions, and measurable performance gains.

EDUCATION/CREDENTIALS:

Associate's Degree or Equivalent Experience

Must Haves:

  • Experience in quality assurance, auditing, utilization review, or a related healthcare operations function.
  • Working knowledge of workers’ compensation utilization review processes and requirements.
  • Ability to interpret and apply client-specific requirements, audit criteria, scoring methodologies, and quality standards.
  • Strong working knowledge of evidence-based and jurisdiction-specific clinical guidelines and criteria, including ODG, MTUS, and other applicable state-specific treatment guidelines.
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to identify trends, investigate discrepancies, and perform root-cause analysis.
  • Ability to translate audit findings and data into practical process improvements and corrective actions.
  • Experience providing quality feedback, coaching, or education to operational teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with internal leadership and external client partners.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to independently manage recurring audits, deadlines, documentation, and follow-up activities.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to work effectively with reporting, audit, and case-management systems.
  • Ability to collaborate across Operations, Quality, Technology, and other functional teams.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years’ experience working with the client(s) the role will support in a QA function

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Prolonged periods sitting or remaining stationary at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Constant operation of a computer, keyboard, mouse, and other digital productivity tools.
  • Close visual acuity required to view computer screens, analyze data, and read extensive digital documentation.
  • Frequent communication with team members, leadership, and external partners via email, chat, phone, and video conferencing platforms.
  • Occasional moving or positioning of office equipment or files weighing up to 10–15 pounds.

Why Join Dane Street?

  • Collaborative remote culture
  • Professional growth opportunities
  • Meaningful work supporting the healthcare industry
  • Comprehensive benefits
  • Great Place to Work Certified since 2021
  • Commitment to employee development

WORK FROM HOME TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Maintaining an uninterrupted internet connection is a requirement of all work from home position.

We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees and make employment decisions based on qualifications, merit, business needs, and without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Benefits

Join our team at Dane Street and enjoy a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and peace of mind. We offer a range of benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family. Additionally, we offer voluntary life insurance options for you, your spouse, and your children. We also offer other voluntary benefits which include hospital indemnity, critical illness, accident indemnity, and pet insurance plans. Employees receive basic life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability coverage at no cost. Our generous paid time off policy ensures you have time to relax and recharge, while our 401k plan with a company match helps you plan for your future. Apple equipment and a media stipend are provided for remote workspace.

About Float

Float is the full-stack platform for Specialty Pharma home infusion. We’re on a mission to make healthcare safer, easier, and more efficient by connecting SuperNurses to home medication visits - moving all care that doesn’t need a hospital to the home.

Float connects nurses with patients so they can get treatments for their chronic conditions in the home rather than going into the overcrowded hospital. Our model benefits all stakeholders - patients get more convenient care, nurses access flexible work for better pay, pharmacies fill more prescriptions, hospitals reduce low-reimbursement admissions, and payors enjoy 12x reduced costs with home-delivered care.

Over the last 5 years, we’ve successfully demonstrated multi-state expansion, validated strong unit economics, and boast remarkable retention of patients, nurses, and pharmacies. We’ve facilitated over 100,000 patient visits with 1,100 nurses and are scaling our platform, team, and operations to serve more geographies and patients.

Float Health is currently recruiting nurses and serving patients in California, Nevada, Arizona, Texas, Washington, Michigan, Indiana, Georgia, and Ohio with several new states on the horizon.

The Role

As a Recurring Care Specialist at Float Health, you will play a vital role in driving operational success and delivering an exceptional customer experience. You’ll be responsible for coordinating nursing care by interfacing with specialty pharmacies, nurses, and patients, and maintaining relationships with all parties throughout the life cycle of a recurring patient. Leveraging various technology platforms, you’ll ensure timely, accurate, and efficient scheduling and communication to support seamless care delivery.

This role requires strong organizational skills, excellent attention to detail, and a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset. You’ll handle high volumes of communication and scheduling tasks — responding to or actioning approximately 40 Zendesk tickets, answering up to 30 phone calls, and scheduling between 10 to 30 patient visits per shift. Your ability to manage these responsibilities efficiently while maintaining a high standard of customer service is critical.

In addition to daily operations, you’ll be encouraged to proactively identify and communicate opportunities for process improvement to maximize team efficiency. Flexibility, adaptability, and a collaborative spirit are essential, as you’ll work cross-functionally with operations, product, and engineering teams to share feedback, unify workflows, and help shape the tools and automation that will drive future scalability.

Who you are

  • You’re flexible and have a learner mindset: we’re a start up, we move fast and are constantly improving.
  • You thrive in urgency: our patients are sometimes discharged directly from the hospital to home visits on short notice, you are a key part of their care delivery.
  • You’re team-oriented: in a remote role, strong teammate connections are more important than ever.
  • You have a strong sense of accountability and integrity: external customers and internal team members will rely on you everyday.

What you’ll do:

  • Use Float Health’s proprietary technology and third-party platforms to schedule nursing visits for patients
  • Respond to and manage approximately 40 Zendesk tickets per shift, ensuring accurate and timely resolution

  • Schedule and confirm 10–30 patient visits per shift with accuracy and empathy

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to track data, share insights, and provide feedback to streamline operations
  • Proactively brainstorm and communicate potential process improvements that enhance team efficiency and scalability
  • Cultivate and maintain effective working relationships with specialty pharmacies and nursing partners

Required skills:

  • 1+ years of experience with medical scheduling
  • Excellent critical thinking and problem-solving abilities
  • Highly organized and capable of managing competing priorities with strong time management
  • Exceptional customer service and communication skills—able to explain complex or sensitive information clearly and empathetically
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team in a dynamic, evolving environment
  • Tech-savvy and confident navigating multiple platforms at once, with a strong interest in learning new tools
  • A mindset geared toward continuous improvement and operational efficiency
  • Prior experience in healthcare or familiarity with medical terminology is strongly preferred

Location and Schedule

Location: This is a fully remote position based in the US. Float operates in the PST time zone.

Employment Type: This is a full time position working 40 hours per week.

Work Hours: This role is likely covering one of these two shifts: Wednesday-Sunday 10a-6p PST or Saturday-Wednesday 10a-6p PST (including the weekend).

Note: You only need to submit one application for this role, even if you see the same position posted in multiple locations.

Benefits:

  • 401k matching
  • Unlimited PTO with minimum days

  • Phone & internet monthly stipend

  • HSA & FSA

Compensation for this role consists of a base salary and options grant, with the base salary expected to range from $48,000 to $50,000 per year. Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience and skills.

We’re a Series A startup looking for individuals who are willing to grow with the team and adapt to our fast-paced, ever changing work environment.

As our nurses boldly do what’s right for our patients, we boldly do what’s right for them. If this is a purpose that inspires you, we’d love to talk!

This person will sit at the intersection of clinical operations, engineering, and the business, turning real member needs into products and features that make a delightful care experience easier to access and more engaging.

As Rezilient scales across new employers, health systems, and markets, this role will bring structure and focus to how product decisions get made: defining problems clearly, prioritizing against measurable outcomes, and shipping in close partnership with Engineering, Clinical Operations, Customer Success, and Sales. The role will also help shape how Rezilient applies AI in care delivery.

Success in this role looks like a clear and trusted roadmap, fast and higher-quality releases, and measurable gains in member engagement and outcomes. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable setting product direction with leadership and working through requirements and edge cases with engineers, and brings sound judgment to a regulated healthcare environment where the ability to both move fast and “do no harm” matter.

Key Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Rezilient member experience, aligning priorities with company goals and customer commitments.
  • Translate input from leadership, clinical teams, customers, and data into a prioritized roadmap with clearly defined outcomes.
  • Communicate roadmap decisions and tradeoffs to stakeholders at every level, from executives to front-line care teams.
  • Ensure products meet HIPAA, security, and healthcare regulatory requirements in partnership with Compliance and Engineering.

Discovery & Requirements

  • Lead product discovery with members and internal stakeholders to understand workflows and pain points.
  • Write clear product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria that Engineering and Design can build against.
  • Partner with Design on user flows, prototypes, and usability testing to validate solutions before and after launch.

Delivery & Launch

  • Partner with Engineering to plan sprints, manage the backlog, and keep delivery on track against committed timelines.
  • Work with Product Operations and QA to ensure releases are well tested, documented, and ready for internal teams.
  • Own launch planning with Clinical Operations, Customer Success, and Implementation so new features roll out smoothly.

Metrics & Continuous Improvement

  • Define product KPIs around member activation, engagement, utilization, and app store reviews, and track them on a consistent cadence.
  • Use product analytics, customer feedback, and operational data to identify opportunities and measure impact.
  • Share regular product updates and insights with leadership and cross-functional partners.
  • Raise the bar for product practice across the team by sharing frameworks, templates, and best practices that help the product function scale.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a product or product area from discovery through launch and iteration.
  • Experience in healthcare, health tech, or consumer health industry.
  • Shipped and scaled at least one consumer mobile health, wellness, or fitness app with a large active user base, with strong product instincts for onboarding, engagement, and retention.
  • Experience building AI or machine learning features into a product.
  • Fluency with AI-enabled productivity tools, and the judgment to know where they help and where direct human research and review remain necessary.
  • Strong skills in writing requirements, prioritizing a backlog, and working day to day with engineering and design teams.
  • A data-driven approach, with comfort defining success metrics and using analytics to guide decisions.
  • Sound judgment and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving, high-growth startup environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with HIPAA, SOC 2, and healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7 and FHIR.
  • Experience with employer benefits, health plans, or B2B2C healthcare models.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Confluence, Notion, Figma, and product analytics platforms.

Benefits

At Rezilient Health, we're on a mission to make humane healthcare truly abundant, and we invest in the people who make that possible. This is a high-impact role where your ideas directly shape how care is delivered, within a supportive, collaborative, and diverse team that believes healthcare is fundamentally a human experience. We back that commitment with a robust total rewards package:

  • Meaningful ownership through stock options, allowing you to share directly in the value you help create as we grow
  • Competitive base compensation
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage options, with Rezilient contributing toward your premiums
  • Complimentary access to Rezilient's clinical programs for you and your household members, the same connected care we deliver to our members
  • 401(k) retirement plan to support your long-term financial well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off, so you can recharge without counting days
  • Dedicated Paid Sick Leave, separate from your FTO, for when health needs come first
  • 11 paid company holidays each year
  • Paid family leave to support you through life's biggest moments
  • Optional ancillary benefits, including life insurance, disability coverage, and a Health Savings Account (HSA)

jobs.excerpt: If you're energized by big opportunities, love building relationships with senior decision-makers, and get a genuine thrill from turning a complex business challenge into a great deal, you might be our next National Account Director.
jobs.description:
If you're energized by big opportunities, love building relationships with senior decision-makers, and get a genuine thrill from turning a complex business challenge into a great deal, you might be our next National Account Director.

As a National Account Director, you'll help bring FloWater to some of the country's largest and most influential organizations, building strategic partnerships that can span multiple locations, teams, and business units.

This is a role for a strategic, relentless sales professional who knows how to open doors, navigate complex organizations, build relationships at the executive level, uncover meaningful business needs, and turn big opportunities into long-term partnerships. You'll own your accounts, build your pipeline, lead complex sales cycles, negotiate meaningful deals, and identify opportunities to grow FloWater's footprint across national and multi-location customers.

About Us:

We believe everyone deserves water they can trust — and actually love drinking. Since 2013, FloWater has been on a mission to transform the way the world drinks water, one Refill Station at a time.

Today, more than 16,000 FloWater Refill Stations across the United States hydrate millions of people every year inside some of the world's biggest and coolest brands in fitness, hospitality, education, and beyond.

We're not just another water company. We're building the most loved water brand in the country and redefining what people expect from drinking water. We move fast, think big, care deeply about our customers and our mission, and believe work should be both meaningful and fun.

What You'll Do:

As a National Account Director, you'll own the strategy and sales process for high-value national and multi-location opportunities — from the first conversation through negotiation, close, implementation, and expansion.

  • Hunt for big opportunities: Identify and pursue high-value national and multi-location prospects using creative prospecting, networking, referrals, industry relationships, events, and other strategies to open doors within target organizations.
  • Build a strategic pipeline: Develop and maintain a healthy pipeline of qualified enterprise opportunities, balancing near-term revenue with longer-term strategic accounts.
  • Own complex sales cycles: Lead opportunities from initial outreach and discovery through presentations, proposals, negotiations, contracting, and close.
  • Build executive relationships: Establish trusted relationships with senior executives, procurement leaders, facilities teams, sustainability leaders, and other key stakeholders across complex organizations.
  • Develop account strategies: Create thoughtful account plans that identify decision-makers, business priorities, opportunities, potential barriers, and paths to expanding FloWater's relationship.
  • Tell the FloWater story: Deliver compelling presentations and business cases that connect FloWater's product, customer experience, sustainability impact, and business value to each organization's unique needs.
  • Create value, not just deals: Understand the customer's business, uncover meaningful challenges, and position FloWater as a strategic solution rather than simply another product or service.
  • Drive expansion: Identify opportunities to grow existing national accounts across additional locations, business units, facilities, and use cases.
  • Navigate the organization: Build relationships across multiple levels of an account and create alignment among stakeholders who influence the purchasing decision.
  • Negotiate and close: Develop proposals, pricing strategies, and commercial solutions and confidently lead negotiations through contract execution.
  • Forecast with discipline: Maintain accurate CRM data, pipeline stages, close dates, and forecasts while providing clear visibility into opportunities, risks, and next steps.
  • Be the customer champion: Partner with Customer Success, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Sales leadership to ensure strategic customers receive a great experience from initial sale through implementation and expansion.
  • Get out there: Travel as needed for executive meetings, customer presentations, industry events, conferences, and other opportunities where being in the room matters.
  • Be a great teammate: Share market intelligence, collaborate across teams, celebrate wins, and help create the kind of team people genuinely enjoy being part of.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

We're looking for someone who is competitive, curious, confident, and energized by making things happen. You'll thrive here if you:

  • 7+ years of successful B2B sales experience, with enterprise, strategic, national, or multi-location accounts.
  • Proven track record of consistently achieving or exceeding sales targets and developing new business.
  • Demonstrated success managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and closing high-value opportunities.
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to build credibility and trusted relationships with senior decision makers.
  • Strong strategic account planning, business development, negotiation, presentation, and communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and execute account expansion and cross-sell opportunities.
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to develop compelling value propositions and ROI-based business cases.
  • Highly organized and disciplined with strong pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM skills.
  • Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating across a growing organization.
  • Self-motivated, entrepreneurial, and results-oriented with a high level of ownership and urgency.
  • Passionate about FloWater’s product, customers, mission, and opportunity to create meaningful business and sustainability impact.
  • Experience selling into national or multi-location organizations.
  • Experience with facilities, workplace, hospitality, education, healthcare, food service, or other distributed-location environments.
  • Experience selling sustainability, workplace, water, environmental, facilities, or technology solutions.
  • Existing relationships with national or enterprise-level decision makers.
  • Experience working in a high-growth or entrepreneurial environment.
  • Willingness to travel nationally to support customer meetings, conferences, trade shows, and other events and activities; must be within 60 miles of a major airport.

Why FloWater?

We work hard, move fast, and believe work should be something you actually enjoy doing. You'll join a team that's passionate about what we're building, celebrates wins, supports each other, and isn't afraid to have some fun along the way.

You'll work with recognizable brands, make an impact at a growing company, and sell a product people genuinely love. And yes — we take hydration seriously. We just don't take ourselves too seriously.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation $125K - $150K (+ commission)
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • FSA
  • 401(k)
  • Partially paid parental leave
  • Paid Time Off
  • The opportunity to work for a growing, mission-driven company that is changing the way people drink water
  • A team that values collaboration, authenticity, big ideas, and getting things done

Ready to Make an Impact?

This role is perfect for someone who is ready to take on a big challenge, build strategic relationships, pursue ambitious goals, and have some fun along the way. If you're a natural relationship builder, a strategic thinker, and someone who knows how to turn big opportunities into lasting partnerships — and you want to sell a product with a purpose — we want to meet you.

Come help us deliver outcomes with impact, one Refill Station at a time.

Our Commitment

At FloWater, we believe people do their best work when they can be their authentic selves. We're committed to creating an inclusive, equitable workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and empowered to contribute, grow, and succeed. FloWater provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected status.

jobs.excerpt: ResponsibilitiesPeraton is seeking an experienced AWS Cloud Security Engineer to design, build, and operate security controls for a FedRAMP Moderate-authorized AWS cloud infrastructure supporting Peraton's RDG (Risk Decision Group) program.
jobs.description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an experienced AWS Cloud Security Engineer to design, build, and operate security controls for a FedRAMP Moderate-authorized AWS cloud infrastructure supporting Peraton's RDG (Risk Decision Group) program. This is a hands-on role with a key part in day-to-day cloud security operations, embedding secure-by-design principles into cloud architecture, and maintaining continuous FedRAMP compliance.

The engineer is responsible for implementing security architecture, hardening cloud environments, maintaining continuous compliance monitoring, and supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience securing AWS environments within a federal compliance framework (FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, RMF, or similar).

This is a 100% remote position.

Responsibilities

  • Design and implement security architecture for AWS workloads aligned with FedRAMP Moderate baseline controls
  • Build and maintain security guardrails using AWS-native services (IAM, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, CloudTrail, KMS, WAF, Macie, Inspector)
  • Implement and manage Infrastructure as Code security controls (Terraform/CloudFormation) with policy as code
  • Support System Security Plans (SSPs), ATO activities, and POA&M remediation
  • Perform continuous monitoring, vulnerability scanning, patch management tracking, and monthly/annual assessment support
  • Configure and maintain centralized logging, SIEM integration, and audit trail retention per FedRAMP/NIST requirements
  • Implement least-privilege IAM policies, service control policies (SCPs), and cross-account access controls.
  • Manage encryption at rest and in transit (KMS, ACM, TLS enforcement) per FIPS 140-2/140-3 requirements where applicable
  • Respond to security incidents, perform root cause analysis, and support cloud-specific incident response playbooks
  • Collaborate with DevOps/Platform teams to embed security into CI/CD pipelines (DevSecOps)
  • Maintain documentation for control implementation statements, architecture diagrams, and audit evidence
  • Support boundary definition and system categorization activities (FIPS 199) as required

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • US citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a Top-Secret eligible clearance
  • Minimum 8 years work experience with BS/BA in computer science, or 10 years work experience with an AA/AS degree in Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 5+ years of hands-on AWS engineering experience, with 3+ years specifically in cloud security roles
  • Demonstrated experience working within a FedRAMP Moderate or FedRAMP High, DoD IL4/IL5, or equivalent federal compliance environment
  • Experience supporting or maintaining an SSP and RMF processes
  • Experience with AWS GovCloud (US), AWS Commercial, or equivalent federal AWS environments
  • Strong hands-on expertise with AWS security services: IAM, GuardDuty, Security Hub, AWS Config, CloudTrail, KMS, WAF, Macie, Inspector, and Systems Manager
  • Solid understanding of NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control families (AC, AU, CM, IA, SC, SI, etc.) and the ability to map implementations to specific controls
  • 3+ years of experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform and/or CloudFormation), including security scanning and policy-as-code tools
  • Networking security fundamentals: VPC design, security groups, NACLs, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, and network segmentation for compliance boundaries
  • Experience with vulnerability management tools (AWS Inspector or similar) and remediation tracking
  • Experience implementing Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) in AWS
  • Familiarity with SIEM/log aggregation tools (Splunk, AWS CloudWatch, OpenSearch, or similar) for security event monitoring
  • Scripting ability in Python or Bash for automating compliance checks and remediation
  • Understanding of encryption standards relevant to federal systems (FIPS 140-2/140-3, TLS 1.2+)
  • One of the following certifications: AWS Certified Security – Specialty, or AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional (with a security focus), or CISSP, CISM, or Security+ (with strong AWS hands-on experience).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience supporting a Peraton program or similar federal integrator (Leidos, Booz Allen, SAIC, General Dynamics IT, etc.)
  • Familiarity with server and systems hardening software
  • Experience with container security (ECS/EKS), including image scanning (ECR scanning) and runtime protection
  • Experience with AWS Control Tower and multi-account landing zone security governance
  • Experience automating compliance evidence collection for continuous ATO (cATO)
  • Prior experience with change management processes in a regulated/audited environment
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related field
  • Active security clearance
  • Experience with AWS AI services (Amazon Bedrock)
  • Experience with hybrid/multi-cloud architecture, including Azure (VNets, Azure AD/Entra ID, Azure Policy, ExpressRoute)
  • Experience with Microsoft .NET
  • Experience supporting ATO/continuous monitoring processes
  • Familiarity with DevSecOps pipelines
  • Familiarity with AI security and governance frameworks, national security/defense/critical infrastructure missions, and supporting federal agencies or large GovCon programs

#RDG

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Target Salary Range

$104,000 - $166,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

EEO

EEO: Equal opportunity employer, including disability and protected veterans, or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Los Angeles, CA, USA
jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Sales Development Representative (North America)

Position Details

Position Title: Sales Development Representative (SDR)
Department: Sales
Division: Sales
Region: North America
Reports to: Director, SMB Sales NA
Direct Reports: None

About Buildxact

Buildxact is construction management software built specifically for residential builders, remodelers, and contractors. We help our customers estimate faster, win more work, and manage projects with confidence.

We're growing quickly across North America and are looking for curious, driven people who enjoy solving problems, learning new industries, and making a measurable impact.

The Opportunity

As a Sales Development Representative at Buildxact, you'll be responsible for creating qualified sales opportunities for our SMB Account Executive team across North America. Although this role is remote, you must be based in either the Austin, TX, or Atlanta, GA, area.

This isn't a traditional SDR role focused purely on activity. We care about outcomes.

You'll combine thoughtful outbound prospecting, buyer intent signals, AI-powered research, and meaningful discovery conversations to engage builders who are most likely to benefit from Buildxact.

In many cases, you'll conduct the initial discovery and may deliver an introductory product walkthrough before handing highly qualified opportunities to an Account Executive. Success is measured by both the number of qualified opportunities you create and the ARR those opportunities generate.

If you're naturally curious, enjoy experimenting, love learning what makes customers tick, and want to build a career in SaaS sales, we'd love to meet you.

What You'll Do

  • Execute multi-channel outbound prospecting campaigns across phone, email, LinkedIn, and video.

  • Prioritize outreach using intent data, trigger events, account research, and buying signals to focus on accounts most likely to convert.

  • Use AI-powered tools to accelerate account research, personalize outreach, prepare for conversations, and improve call quality.

  • Conduct structured discovery conversations to understand a builder's business, current processes, challenges, and goals.

  • Where appropriate, deliver an introductory Buildxact product walkthrough to validate fit before handing the opportunity to an Account Executive.

  • Partner closely with Account Executives to ensure seamless opportunity handoffs with complete discovery notes, qualification details, and customer context.

  • Maintain accurate CRM records in Salesforce and manage prospecting activities within Outreach (or similar sales engagement platforms).

  • Continuously test and improve messaging, sequencing, and outreach strategies while sharing insights with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Revenue Operations.

  • Report on pipeline activity, conversion rates, qualified opportunities, and sourced ARR.

  • Gather and share market intelligence, customer feedback, competitive insights, and Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) trends.

  • Clearly communicate Buildxact's value proposition in a way that resonates with builders and addresses their specific business challenges.

What Success Looks Like

You'll be successful in this role by:

  • Consistently generating qualified sales opportunities.

  • Contributing meaningful sourced ARR.

  • Delivering high-quality discovery that results in strong AE conversion rates.

  • Maintaining disciplined pipeline management and CRM hygiene.

  • Continuously improving outreach effectiveness through testing and data-driven learning.

  • Becoming a trusted partner to both our customers and internal sales team.

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 1+ years of experience in Sales Development, Business Development, Lead Generation, or B2B sales (SaaS preferred).

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.

  • Ability to quickly learn new industries, products, and customer personas.

  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment while collaborating across teams.

  • Experience using CRM platforms such as Salesforce and sales engagement tools such as Outreach or similar.

  • Comfortable leveraging AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve research, personalization, and productivity.

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling SaaS solutions.

  • Experience within construction, trades, home building, or related industries.

  • Bachelor's degree (not required).

What Makes You Great

We're looking for someone who is:

  • Curious — You enjoy learning about customers, industries, and new technology.

  • Coachable — You actively seek feedback and apply it quickly.

  • Experiment-driven — You enjoy testing new messaging and finding what works.

  • Resilient — You stay motivated through high-volume outreach and rejection.

  • Customer-focused — You ask thoughtful questions and uncover real business challenges.

  • Collaborative — You work closely with AEs and cross-functional teams to improve results.

  • Self-motivated — You take ownership of your pipeline and consistently execute.

Working at Buildxact

Buildxact currently operates with a remote-first work model. From time to time, team members may be asked to attend in-person meetings or team events. Your manager will work with you to determine expectations based on business needs.

Career Growth

High-performing SDRs have opportunities to progress into roles such as:

  • Account Executive (SMB)

  • Business Development Manager

  • Customer Success Manager

Promotion into an Account Executive position is earned through sustained performance against qualified opportunity and ARR targets, demonstration of AE-level sales skills, and business need.

Health & Safety

All employees are responsible for contributing to a safe and healthy workplace by identifying, reporting, and helping control workplace hazards, and by promptly reporting any accidents or incidents.

Our Values

At Buildxact, our values guide how we work every day:

  • It's Yours to Nail

  • Customer Success is Our Success

  • Do What's Right

  • Keep It Simple
