Job Summary:

Mercer Advisors is looking for a rare operator — someone who can think strategically, move fast, and get a lot done. As VP of Sales Enablement and Operations, you'll sit at the center of one of the most ambitious client development builds in the wealth management industry, responsible for three of the most critical levers in our growth engine. This is a purpose-built role designed for where we are going — not a backfill — created to bring structure, visibility, and momentum to a Growth organization that spans Client Development and Marketing.

This is not a role for someone who manages from a distance. You'll roll up your sleeves every single day — building roadmaps, coordinating conversion programs, running operating rhythms, and leading a high-performing central Revenue Operations and Enablement team. You bring clarity to complexity, urgency to problems, and follow-through to everything you touch.

You'll directly lead the Central Revenue Operations and Enablement team — a four-person team that spans both operational infrastructure and field enablement. Beyond your direct team, you'll orchestrate the broader network of shared services and program managers who keep the Client Development organization running. You'll also serve as a key operating partner within the broader Growth leadership team, which spans Client Development and Marketing program leads. This VP role facilitates and operationalizes decisions — you bring visibility, sequencing, and follow-through. Decision authority sits with Growth leadership.

Essential Job Functions for this role include:

Orchestrate the Value Creation and Program Roadmap

● Own the master roadmap for the Growth organization — tracking all active programs and projects across Client Development, Growth programs, and shared services, sequencing rollouts, and ensuring shared resources are applied in the right order.

● Portfolio governance: own intake, visibility, sequencing, and capacity management across initiatives — facilitating prioritization decisions with Growth leadership, not making them unilaterally

● Partner with program managers and shared services teams across the broader Growth organization — including initiatives that span Client Development, Marketing, Technology, and Analytics — to facilitate cross-functional coordination, align priorities, remove dependencies, and ensure initiatives progress efficiently

● Maintain a live view of what's in flight, what's at risk, and what needs a decision — surfacing that picture to leadership clearly and consistently

Own the Operating Cadence for the Client Development Team

● Design and own the meeting cadences, agendas, and operating rituals that keep the Client Development organization aligned and moving forward

● Ensure the right conversations happen at the right time — weekly team syncs, monthly program reviews, quarterly roadmap sessions, and annual planning cycles

● Track key initiatives across the organization, ensuring accountability, follow-through, and visibility for senior leadership

● Produce clear, concise leadership updates and board-ready materials that reflect the state of the Client Development organization

Lead the Revenue Operations and Enablement Team

● Directly manage 4 members of the Revenue Operations and Enablement team — spanning both operational infrastructure and field enablement — providing clear direction, active coaching, and a culture of high performance

● Set priorities for the central revenue operations team on a weekly and quarterly basis — ensuring the team is working on the highest-leverage activities

● Build a team that operates with urgency, precision, and a bias for action — you set the standard and model it every day

● Drive execution through structured two-week sprints — keeping the team focused on the highest-priority work, moving with urgency, and maintaining clear accountability for what gets done each cycle

● RVP onboarding and training — your team builds and owns the onboarding experience that gets new RVPs productive quickly and aligned to how we work

● Rolling out new capabilities — serve as the deployment lead for new tools, programs, and processes, ensuring field teams understand, adopt, and leverage what's being launched

● Driving change management — lead the people side of significant organizational shifts, including new technology rollouts, compensation plan changes, and territory design

● Partner with the Head of Client Development to grow the Revenue Operations and Enablement function over time, making the case for investment where it's needed

Own the Conversion Improvement Roadmap

● Own the conversion improvement roadmap — a prioritized, sequenced, and living view of what's being worked on, what's at risk, and what needs a decision to move forward

● Drive cross-program coordination across all conversion drivers — Proposals, Training, High Value Opportunities, and Performance Coaching — ensuring these programs are sequenced well, not working at cross-purposes, and that blockers get surfaced and resolved quickly

● Partner with the data analytics team — who own full-funnel conversion reporting — to stay current on conversion trends, risks, and program-level performance, and translate that data into clear leadership updates that identify where the system needs attention

● Talk regularly to the field — RVPs, Managing Directors, and advisors — to understand what's holding up conversion in real time, and bring those insights back to the program leads who own the levers

This role owns the roadmap, the coordination, the visibility, and the follow-through — ensuring the system is working even when no single person owns the whole thing

● Surface blockers quickly and clearly — escalating where decisions are needed, and ensuring nothing stalls because the right people weren't in the room

● Report on conversion progress, trends, and opportunities to Growth leadership on a regular cadence — producing a clear, concise picture of where we stand and what needs attention

This professional role requires availability during standard business hours of Monday through Friday from 8AM to 5PM. At times, the role may have early or late hours to meet business tasks and deadlines for external and internal client needs.

All roles classified as a non-exempt are required to record working time into the timekeeping system daily at the start and end of each workday plus a 30-minute unpaid lunch period.

jobs.title: Consultant: Ring-Fencing Mining Income: A toolkit for tax administrators and pol
jobs.excerpt: The International Institute for Sustainable Development is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges.
jobs.description:
The International Institute for Sustainable Development is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. 

IISD hosts the Secretariat of the Intergovernmental Forum on Mining, Minerals, Metals and Sustainable Development (IGF).

The IGF's Global Mining Tax Initiative (GMTI) helps countries to increase mining revenues for sustainable development. Drawing on broad experience working with IGF member governments, the Secretariat offers this specialized and comprehensive program covering fiscal policy for the entire mining value chain, from exploration and development to mining, processing, mineral sales, and mine closure. The GMTI focuses on all aspects of fiscal policy, including taxes, royalties, and financial modelling, and has developed particular expertise on the fiscal treatment of mineral beneficiation and downstream processing.

Background

In 2025, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the IGF jointly published Ring-Fencing Mining Income: A Toolkit for Tax Administrators and Policy-Makers, a comprehensive practice note on when and how governments should limit the consolidation of income and expenditure across mining projects and activities. The toolkit addresses the treatment of integrated operations in several places, notably its discussion of ring-fencing by shared processing facility, ring-fencing of upstream versus downstream activities, and its recommendation that transfer pricing rules extend to internal dealings within a single ring-fenced entity.

The toolkit's treatment of integration is oriented toward the design of the ring-fencing rule itself: where the statutory boundary should sit when a mine feeds a processor, and how to prevent profit-shifting across that boundary once drawn. There is a separate but distinct question to consider, namely how ring-fencing rules interact with the value-addition (beneficiation) tax and non-tax incentives that many of the same governments offer to draw investment into downstream processing. Specifically, this would include such incentives as tax holidays, accelerated depreciation, royalty rate differentials for refined versus unrefined product, and preferential processing licences. Where such incentives sit on one side of a ring-fence and the extraction activity sits on the other, the incentive may fail to achieve its stated purpose (because start-up losses in the incentivized processing segment cannot offset profits in the ring-fenced mining segment), or it may create the very transfer-pricing and rate-arbitrage risks the toolkit is designed to guard against.

The Challenge

Tax policy-makers and administrators currently have authoritative guidance on ring-fencing design (the 2025 toolkit), and there is separate literature on mineral beneficiation incentives (such as from the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, International Council on Mining and Metals tax expenditure work), but there is no practice note that puts the two together: a framework for how a value-addition incentive should be designed, and where the ring-fence should sit, when the two instruments apply to the same integrated project. This gap matters because the interaction is not merely theoretical. It shows up directly in country practice already surveyed by the toolkit and by the IGF's own country work: a differentiated corporate income tax rate for mining versus mineral processing licences, a statutory carve-out permitting pooled treatment of “inseparable or substantially interdependent” integrated beneficiation operations, and processing facilities sited in export processing zones specifically to capture preferential tax treatment.

Our Response

The IGF seeks to develop a practice note on the ring-fencing implications of mining value-addition incentives for integrated mining projects, in continuation of the 2025 Ring-Fencing Mining Income toolkit. The note will take the toolkit's existing design guidance on integrated operations as its starting point and extend it to address the incentive-interaction question: how should a ring-fencing regime be designed, and how should a value-addition incentive be designed, so that the two are coherent rather than potentially working against each other on the same integrated project?

The country case set will be determined jointly with the consultant at inception stage. Candidates must include jurisdictions that illustrate materially different design choices. Such design choices include a statutory integration test permitting pooled treatment of extraction and processing under common control, a differentiated tax rate between mining and processing licences, strict project-level ring-fencing with value addition pursued through the royalty schedule rather than through ring-fencing relief, and vertical integration achieved through trade policy (export restriction) rather than through the ring-fencing rule as such. Ghana and Tanzania are both covered in the toolkit's shared-processing-facility and upstream/downstream discussions and are also considered as candidates in this study because they build directly on documented toolkit examples rather than introducing an unrelated set of countries.

Deliverable – Technical Input for the Ring-Fencing and Value Addition Practice Note

The IGF seeks a consultant, or small consultant team, with expertise in mining fiscal policy and comparative tax law to conduct desk-based research and support the drafting of the practice note. The work is weighted toward legal and literature research rather than field consultation. The consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

  1. Prepare a short inception note proposing the for IGF's confirmation, with rationale, together with the analytical framework to be applied consistently across cases (a typology of ring-fencing design and a ) and confirming how the note's structure will map onto and extend the relevant sections of the 2025 toolkit.
  2. Examine country cases where ring-fencing rules separate upstream mining and downstream processing activities alongside policies or incentives designed to attract investment in downstream value addition. Assess how these frameworks interact in practice, identify any implementation challenges or unintended consequences, and draw on discussions with government officials and other stakeholders to understand how these issues are being managed.
  3. For each case study country, undertake a primary-source review of the relevant mining code, income tax act, royalty legislation, and any special licensing regime, to establish: (a) how the ring-fence is legally defined; (b) whether and how integrated extraction-processing operations are treated differently from stand-alone projects; (c) what value-addition incentive, if any, applies to the processing stage and how it is designed (rate differential, holiday, accelerated allowance, integration carve-out); (d) how transfer pricing between ring-fenced segments is regulated; and (e) whether case law or administrative guidance has tested the boundary.
  4. Identify, for each country, at least one integrated project that illustrates how the ring-fencing rule and the value-addition incentive have applied together in practice, including any documented disputes with the revenue authority over the mining/processing boundary or over the incentive's effect.[
  5. Where available, compile documented estimates or reasonable proxies for the fiscal cost of the relevant value-addition incentive and any evidence on whether it changed investment or beneficiation outcomes, flagging data gaps.
  6. Where the desk research leaves material gaps, conduct light-touch validation (by email or short call) with country officials and practitioners to confirm interpretation of the legal provisions.

Timelines

  1. Inception note proposing the country case set, analytical framework, and legal sources. Due: November 2026. Estimated effort: 5 days.
  2. Literature review and typology synthesis. Due: November 2026. Estimated effort: 5 days.
  3. Primary legal-source review and case mapping for all confirmed countries. Due: November 2026. Estimated effort: 5 days.
  4. First draft and review of the report. Due: December 2026. Estimated effort: 10 days.
  5. Finalization of findings in the final draft report. Due: December 2026. Estimated effort: 5 days.

Location: Remote

IISD will not apply for residency and work permits for this position on behalf of the applicant.

Candidates must hold appropriate work authorization for locations where they expect to be based.

Application Process

Application deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until filled.

This is a consultant position. Submissions must be in English.

To apply for this consultancy, interested applicants should submit the following:

  • A CV (detailing your experience with mining fiscal policy, tax expenditure analysis, or mineral beneficiation policy).
  • An expression of interest (one page), including proposed approach and, where relevant, proposed country case set and coverage by team member if submitting as a team.

NOTE:

  • Incomplete applications will be automatically disqualified.
  • Only those candidates IISD wishes to interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
Une version en langue française suit

About the role:

Gartner Analysts are industry thought leaders who create must-have insights, market predictions and best practices for a broad range of world-leading organizations. A Senior Director serves as a leader within Gartner’s Business and Technology Insights (BTI) group, establishing oneself as a credible voice within their designated market at local, regional and global levels. Utilizing exceptional research and analytical skills, a Senior Director plays a significant role in producing pragmatic and provocative insights which Gartner clients consume and apply to propel their business toward key objectives. They are a trusted source of advice for clients, reinforcing Gartner’s value every day by engaging them via in-person meetings, virtual meetings, sales support visits and Gartner conferences to discuss complex client challenges and offer appropriate recommendations.


This role sits within Gartner’s Software Engineering Practice and advises leaders of software engineering organizations around the world. The focus is on helping organizations effectively apply AI and agentic capabilities across the SDLC and in the software they deliver to drive new sources of value. The role provides strategic guidance on how to develop a comprehensive software engineering AI strategy, prioritize high-value opportunities, and measure and communicate the impact of AI to drive ROI.


What you will do:

  • Create innovative, thought provoking, and highly leveraged “must-have insights” content
  • Develop new insights and ideas through thought leadership and offer compelling, actionable approaches to client's needs and requests that accelerate the client's ability to act
  • Develop in-depth analysis to identify the root cause of a client’s barriers or overall needs and reframe thinking to drive strategy forward
  • Demonstrate thought leadership in establishing Insights positions across a team of analysts
  • Bring provocative, independent insights to Gartner leaders that can evolve the course of a research agenda
  • Research, analyze and predict market trends and shifts to provide clients and vendors with actionable insights
  • Provide clients and prospects with actionable advice aligned to their designated content area via virtual or face-to-face interactions
  • Create and deliver high value presentation materials on and off stage for Gartner events, industry and professional association conferences, and client briefings
  • Support BTI and Sales: Provide sales support serving as voice of the market to help Insights teams create content and to drive engagement with clients to make progress against their critical priorities to grow their business
  • Provide high quality and timely content peer review
  • Build credibility as an industry expert to represent Gartner insights, methodology and strategy
  • Actively participate in innovation, ideation, and research discussions and collaborate effectively with peers in the Insights community
  • Identify research process improvements or develop new processes that help the team and BTI provide excellent service delivery
  • Be a mentor and a coach by supporting more junior team members
  • Be client-centric while actively seeking to help clients engage regularly and often with Gartner insights and interactions

What you will need:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; Graduate degree preferred
  • 12+ years of relevant field or industry experience
  • Proven software engineering leadership experience, having led large-scale, multi-team software delivery organizations with accountability for execution, quality and outcomes
  • Deep expertise in software engineering strategy and value measurement for AI, including roadmap planning, technology decision-making, performance assessment, metrics and ROI evaluation.
  • Hands-on expertise in AI-native software development, including embedding AI across the SDLC, leveraging AI to improve developer productivity and optimizing software delivery outcomes, and AI engineering to deliver AI applications and agents.
  • Demonstrate executive presence; can immediately establish credibility with executives and additional stakeholders
  • Strong organizational skills; ability to work under tight deadlines and produce high quality deliverables
  • Demonstrate excellence in research and writing ability
  • Strong written and verbal proficiency, analytical and presentation skills; ability to engage clients and respond effectively to questions
  • Proficient in analyzing and synthesizing data; can effectively apply patterns and frameworks while drawing and defending conclusions to client challenges
  • Strong communication skills - able to explain complex concepts concisely and simply
  • Subject matter expertise; comfortable presenting at large and small-scale speaking engagements
  • Strong business and financial acumen
  • Deep knowledge of the global and competitive landscape within subject area as well as the interplay in that market
  • Ability to work independently, while also being intrinsically motivated to collaborate across teams and support the workflow of others, in a multicultural global team
  • Learning agile and adept with navigating highly matrixed environments
  • Ability to represent Gartner's research methodology and strategies effectively at all levels
  • Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% (where applicable)
  • Fluency in written and spoken English is required as this role requires daily communication in English with clients and colleagues located in other provinces and in the United States.

À propos du rôle :

Les analystes de Gartner sont des chefs de file de l’industrie qui créent des analyses incontournables, des prédictions de marché et des meilleures pratiques pour un vaste éventail d’organisations de premier plan à l’échelle mondiale. Un directeur principal agit à titre de chef de file au sein du groupe Business and Technology Insights (BTI) de Gartner, s’imposant comme une voix crédible au sein de son marché désigné aux niveaux local, régional et mondial. En s’appuyant sur des compétences exceptionnelles en recherche et en analyse, un directeur principal joue un rôle significatif dans la production d’analyses pragmatiques et stimulantes que les clients de Gartner consomment et appliquent pour propulser leur entreprise vers leurs objectifs clés. Ils constituent une source de conseils de confiance pour les clients, renforçant la valeur de Gartner au quotidien en échangeant avec eux lors de réunions en personne, de réunions virtuelles, de visites de soutien aux ventes et de conférences Gartner afin de discuter de défis complexes et d’offrir des recommandations appropriées.

Ce poste s’inscrit au sein de la pratique d’ingénierie logicielle de Gartner et conseille les dirigeants d’organisations d’ingénierie logicielle à travers le monde. L’objectif principal est d’aider les organisations à appliquer efficacement l’intelligence artificielle et les capacités agentiques tout au long du cycle de vie du développement logiciel (SDLC) ainsi que dans les logiciels qu’elles livrent afin de générer de nouvelles sources de valeur. Ce rôle fournit des conseils stratégiques sur la façon d’élaborer une stratégie globale d’IA en ingénierie logicielle, de prioriser les opportunités à haute valeur ajoutée, ainsi que de mesurer et communiquer l’impact de l’IA afin de stimuler le retour sur investissement (ROI).


Ce que vous ferez :

  • Créer du contenu innovant, stimulant la réflexion et à fort levier (« analyses incontournables »).
  • Développer de nouvelles perspectives et idées grâce au leadership éclairé et offrir des approches convaincantes et concrètes répondant aux besoins et demandes des clients afin d'accélérer leur capacité d’action.
  • Réaliser des analyses approfondies pour identifier la cause fondamentale des obstacles ou des besoins globaux d’un client, et recadrer la réflexion afin de faire avancer la stratégie.
  • Faire preuve de leadership éclairé en établissant des prises de position d’analyse au sein d’une équipe d’analystes.
  • Apporter aux dirigeants de Gartner des analyses indépendantes et stimulantes susceptibles de faire évoluer l’orientation d’un programme de recherche.
  • Rechercher, analyser et prédire les tendances et les transformations du marché afin de fournir aux clients et aux fournisseurs des informations concrètes.
  • Fournir aux clients et prospects des conseils pratiques alignés sur leur domaine de contenu désigné, par le biais d’interactions virtuelles ou en personne.
  • Créer et présenter du matériel de présentation à haute valeur ajoutée, sur scène et hors scène, lors d’événements Gartner, de conférences d'associations sectorielles et professionnelles, et de séances d’information destinées aux clients.
  • Soutenir BTI et les ventes : Fournir un soutien aux ventes en servant de voix du marché pour aider les équipes d’analyse à créer du contenu et stimuler l’engagement auprès des clients afin qu'ils progressent vers leurs priorités stratégiques et fassent croître leur entreprise.
  • Effectuer des révisions par les pairs de contenu, de haute qualité et dans les délais impartis.
  • Renforcer sa crédibilité en tant qu'expert du secteur afin de représenter les analyses, la méthodologie et la stratégie de Gartner.
  • Participer activement aux discussions sur l’innovation, l’idéation et la recherche, et collaborer efficacement avec ses pairs de la communauté d’analyse.
  • Identifier des améliorations aux processus de recherche ou développer de nouveaux processus aidant l’équipe et BTI à assurer une prestation de services excellente.
  • Agir à titre de mentor et de coach en appuyant les membres plus juniors de l’équipe.
  • Adopter une approche axée sur le client tout en cherchant activement à aider les clients à faire appel régulièrement et fréquemment aux analyses et interactions de Gartner.

Ce dont vous aurez besoin :

  • Baccalauréat ou expérience équivalente; diplôme d'études supérieures de deuxième ou troisième cycle de préférence.
  • Plus de 12 ans d'expérience pertinente dans le domaine ou le secteur d'activité.
  • Expérience éprouvée en leadership de l’ingénierie logicielle, ayant dirigé des organisations de livraison de logiciels à grande échelle et multi-équipes avec la responsabilité de l’exécution, de la qualité et des résultats.
  • Expertise approfondie de la stratégie d’ingénierie logicielle et de la mesure de la valeur de l’IA, y compris la planification de feuilles de route, la prise de décisions technologiques, l'évaluation de la performance, les indicateurs et l'évaluation du retour sur investissement (ROI).
  • Expertise pratique du développement logiciel natif en IA, y compris l'intégration de l'IA tout au long du SDLC, l'utilisation de l'IA pour améliorer la productivité des développeurs et l'optimisation des résultats de livraison de logiciels, ainsi que l'ingénierie de l'IA pour livrer des applications et des agents d'IA.
  • Présence exécutive démontrée; capacité à établir immédiatement une crédibilité auprès des cadres dirigeants et des autres parties prenantes.
  • Fortes compétences organisationnelles; capacité à travailler selon des échéanciers serrés et à produire des livrables de haute qualité.
  • Excellence démontrée dans la capacité de recherche et de rédaction.
  • Forte maîtrise écrite et verbale, compétences analytiques et de présentation; capacité à susciter l’engagement des clients et à répondre efficacement aux questions.
  • Compétence dans l’analyse et la synthèse de données; capacité à appliquer efficacement des modèles et des cadres de référence tout en tirant et en défendant des conclusions face aux défis des clients.
  • Fortes compétences en communication - capable d’expliquer des concepts complexes de manière concise et simple.
  • Expertise thématique; à l’aise pour effectuer des présentations lors de conférences de petite et grande envergure.
  • Sens aigu des affaires et des finances.
  • Connaissance approfondie du paysage mondial et concurrentiel dans son domaine d’expertise ainsi que des interactions sur ce marché.
  • Capacité à travailler de manière autonome, tout en étant intrinsèquement motivé à collaborer entre les équipes et à appuyer le flux de travail des autres, au sein d’une équipe mondiale multiculturelle.
  • Agilité d’apprentissage et aptitudes à évoluer dans des environnements fortement matriciels.
  • Capacité à représenter efficacement la méthodologie de recherche et les stratégies de Gartner à tous les niveaux.
  • Volonté et capacité de voyager jusqu’à 25 % du temps (selon le cas).
  • La maîtrise de l’anglais écrit et parlé est requise, puisque ce poste exige une communication quotidienne en anglais avec des clients et des collègues situés dans d’autres provinces et aux États-Unis.

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. jobs.description:
About the Role

Sophos is seeking a Global Solutions Engineer to provide senior technical leadership across two strategic growth areas: our Managed Security Service Provider program and our expanding portfolio of AI security solutions. This is a highly visible individual contributor role for someone who can combine deep cybersecurity expertise, hands-on technical capability, partner engagement, and strong business acumen.

In this role, you will help MSSP partners design, launch, and scale differentiated managed security services powered by Sophos technologies. You will also serve as a global subject matter expert for Sophos AI security solutions, helping customers and partners understand, evaluate, and secure the use of AI across modern environments.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable leading executive-level technical conversations, advising SOC and security engineering teams, building labs and demonstrations, supporting proofs of value, and translating complex cybersecurity and AI concepts into clear business outcomes.

What You Will Do

    MSSP Program Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the primary Solutions Engineer for Sophos’ global MSSP program and strategic partner opportunities.
  • Lead technical discovery, solution design, architecture workshops, demonstrations, and proofs of value with MSSP partners.
  • Help partners design and scale managed security services using Sophos Fusion and the broader Sophos cybersecurity portfolio.
  • Advise partners on service architecture, integrations, automation, operational readiness, and repeatable service delivery.

    • AI Security Domain Leadership

  • Act as a global subject matter expert for Sophos AI security solutions, including AI Defense and future AI offerings.
  • Lead demonstrations, workshops, and proofs of value that help customers and partners evaluate AI security risks and solutions.
  • Build hands-on AI security demos, lab environments, attack simulations, and repeatable technical evaluation methods.
  • Share field and market insights with Product, Engineering, Product Marketing, and go-to-market teams.

    • Global Leadership and Field Impact

  • Create reusable technical assets, enablement materials, service blueprints, and field-ready best practices.
  • Mentor Sales Engineers, partner engineers, and other technical stakeholders to strengthen global field capability.
  • Represent Sophos in customer briefings, partner events, webinars, technical communities, and industry forums.
  • Build trusted-advisor relationships with partners, customers, security leaders, and technical decision-makers.

What You Will Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, Security Architecture, security consulting, MSSP engineering, or a similar customer-facing cybersecurity role.
  • Experience supporting MSSP sales, partner engagements, service architecture, or managed security service development.
  • Strong knowledge of modern security operations, including MDR, XDR, SIEM, SOAR, endpoint security, cloud security, threat detection, incident response, and security integrations.
  • Deep understanding of MSSP business and technical models, including the requirements for delivering repeatable services to multiple customers.
  • Strong understanding of artificial intelligence, generative AI systems, AI application architectures, and the security risks associated with adopting and operating AI technologies.
  • Hands-on experience deploying, configuring, integrating, operating, and troubleshooting cybersecurity products and tools.
  • Experience building labs, demonstrations, workshops, proofs of value, and technical validation environments.
  • Ability to work with APIs, automation, cloud platforms, modern application architectures, Linux and Windows environments, networking, identity systems, and security telemetry.
  • Exceptional technical discovery, consultative selling, presentation, storytelling, demonstration, and written communication skills.
  • Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional technical engagements with partners, customers, and internal teams across multiple regions.
  • Willingness and ability to travel up to 50% across North America and internationally.

    • Nice to Have

  • Direct experience working in a Security Operations Center, security engineering organization, incident response team, or cybersecurity leadership role.
  • Experience designing, operating, or bringing managed security services to market.
  • Experience with scripting and automation using Python, PowerShell, Bash, APIs, or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with cloud AI platforms, AI agents, model APIs, local or private models, open-source AI technologies, containers, Kubernetes, and DevSecOps practices.
  • Experience speaking at industry events, publishing technical content, or representing an organization as a cybersecurity subject matter expert.
  • Relevant cybersecurity, cloud, architecture, or AI certifications.
  • Experience with Sophos technologies.

Why Sophos

    Sophos helps organizations and service providers reduce cyber risk through an integrated portfolio of cybersecurity technologies, managed security services, threat intelligence, and expert-led security operations.

    As a Global Solutions Engineer, you will help shape how MSSPs build the next generation of managed security services while contributing to emerging AI security solutions that help customers and partners adopt AI securely. This is an opportunity to combine hands-on engineering, strategic partner engagement, product influence, public thought leadership, and global field impact in a role with meaningful visibility and scope.

Overview

At ALTOUR, we believe people are the driving force behind every meaningful connection - our clients’ and our own. With more than 1,000 team members and a presence in over 80 countries, we are a globally recognized leader in corporate travel management and a proud division of Internova Travel Group, the highest-ranking American corporate travel management company (Business Travel News).

Our mission is to manage the complexities of connecting people so they can represent their brands in the most impactful way possible. That same philosophy shapes our workplace culture, one that evolves, improves, and empowers our people to grow and thrive.

We embrace innovation and leading-edge technology to create smarter, faster, and more tailored solutions - not just for our clients, but for each other. At ALTOUR, you’ll be part of a collaborative, forward-thinking environment where your voice matters and your success is a shared journey. Click here for more information about Altour.

Responsibilities

JOB OVERVIEW

This strategic, high-impact role leads complex venue sourcing projects that deliver cost savings, align with client business objectives, and contribute to overall event success. The individual in this role sources hotels and venues, negotiates contracts, and tracks financial impact, ensuring alignment with client goals and budget requirements. This position collaborates closely with account managers, sales, finance, and meeting planners to ensure a seamless hand-off for execution. Success requires a combination of operational excellence and strategic thinking to drive client satisfaction, high-quality results, and strong financial performance for ALTOUR.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead venue sourcing for complex, high-value client meetings and events

    • Ensure timely and accurate data entry in Cvent and other internal systems
    • Provide financial inputs to support project close-out

Stay current on sourcing trends and mentor others

  • Foster a positive, collaborative team environment
  • Motivate and influence peers to achieve business goals

Serve as a sourcing subject matter expert and informal mentor, leading skill-share sessions and supporting onboarding or upskilling of junior teammates.

Qualifications

Education and Experience:

  • 3-4 years planning high profile programs, preferably with sourcing focus
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent work experience

Skills and Competencies:

Strategic Project Execution & Sourcing Expertise

  • Deep understanding of meetings and incentive planning with a strong focus on venue sourcing
  • Ability to align sourcing strategy with client business objectives, brand standards, and budget parameters
  • Proven ability to manage multiple, high-complexity projects with competing priorities and deadlines
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail to ensure accuracy in budgets, proposals, and reporting
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity and solving problems under tight timelines

Client Engagement & Interpersonal Skills

  • Skilled at building trust with clients, including senior stakeholders and executive-level contacts
  • Exceptional negotiation and communication skills; able to balance client priorities with business needs
  • Collaborative team player who thrives in a cross-functional environment while also working independently
  • Passion for mentorship and knowledge-sharing to support team development and performance growth

Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

Bonus

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

jobs.excerpt: About the TeamDoorDash is one of the world’s leading on-demand logistics platforms.
jobs.description:
About the Team

DoorDash is one of the world’s leading on-demand logistics platforms. Across DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt, our operations span more than 40 countries, dozens of offices, and tens of thousands of employees.Global Safety and Security helps protect our people, property, operations, brand, and reputation across that footprint, using technology, agility, and a people-first approach to stay ahead of evolving risks. Within the team, Protective Services focuses on the safety of our executives, their families, and the operations that support them. Our detection engineering function brings together enterprise, marketplace, open-source, and physical security signals to identify threats that don’t fit neatly within a traditional SOC boundary. This role builds the detection capabilities that turn those signals into timely, actionable intelligence - and helps Protective Services find what matters before it becomes something bigger.

About the Role

Detection engineering looks a little different here.

As a Detection Engineer on Protective Services, you’ll build the technical capabilities that help identify and investigate threats to protected individuals. The signals you’re looking for won’t live neatly in one place—they may surface across identities and endpoints, cloud environments, marketplace activity, support interactions, physical access events, or open-source information.

You’ll connect those signals to find what matters. That means building detections, enrichment, and automation; separating meaningful risk from noise; and investigating what you uncover alongside Protective Services partners.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you’ll work across code, queries, data pipelines, detection repositories, and production systems. You’ll take detections from an initial hypothesis through deployment and tuning, then use what happens in the real world to make them better.

You’ll have ownership of well-understood problems while partnering with senior engineers when the technical complexity, evidence, or potential impact calls for deeper judgment.

This role reports to the Engineering Manager, Protective Services, and participates in an on-call rotation.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Translate threat intelligence, incidents, investigative needs, and observed behavior into production detections that surface meaningful risk, reduce noise, and provide actionable context.
  • Build, test, deploy, tune, and maintain detections and supporting pipelines using source-controlled engineering practices designed to operate reliably at scale.
  • Correlate signals across enterprise telemetry, marketplace activity, physical security events, OSINT, support interactions, and other relevant data to identify and prioritize potential threats.
  • Apply rules, statistical methods, machine learning, and LLM-based techniques where they improve detection quality, prioritization, or investigative context.
  • Investigate detections by querying and correlating data, validating hypotheses, and assessing confidence, scope, and potential impact in partnership with Protective Services.
  • Follow detections through investigation and resolution, using outcomes, false positives, missed indicators, and investigative friction to continuously improve detection logic, tooling, and workflows.
  • Contribute to technical reviews, testing, documentation, standards, and automation that strengthen the reliability and maintainability of the detection function.
  • Participate in on-call and support major investigations, clearly communicating the confidence and limitations of available signals.

We’re excited about you because you have…

  • 3+ years of experience in detection engineering, threat hunting, incident response, security operations engineering, technical threat intelligence, or software engineering applied to security problems.
  • Experience contributing to production detection pipelines using source control, testing, review, deployment, and monitoring practices.
  • Proficiency in SQL or a security query language and the ability to write maintainable code in Python, Go, or another relevant language.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to explore unfamiliar datasets, assess data quality, troubleshoot across systems, and turn threat information into testable detection hypotheses.
  • Experience triaging alerts and investigations, correlating signals across data sources, assessing confidence and scope, and clearly communicating what the evidence supports.
  • Experience building detections or conducting investigations using security, behavioral, or other relevant telemetry. Exposure to identity, endpoint, cloud, marketplace, physical security, OSINT, or unstructured data is a plus.
  • Experience using automation or analytics to improve detection and investigation workflows; familiarity with machine learning or LLM-based techniques is a plus.
  • Familiarity with frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK or D3FEND and their use in organizing detection coverage and identifying gaps.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, investigative, and response teams and handle sensitive information appropriately.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience with Snowflake, Cortex, or Google SecOps is preferred.

We expect this position to be filled by 28 November 2026.

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See below for paid time off details:

  • For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
  • For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

jobs.excerpt: About Generation:At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives.
jobs.description:
About Generation:

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high-priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 150,000+ graduates and 23,000+ employers across 50 professions and 17 countries.

When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have an 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1.9 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 52% are female, 28% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.

About the role:

The Regional Business & Program Development Associate will support the identification, design, and launch of new training and employment programs in high-growth sectors across Latin America.

This role is responsible for conducting labor market research, analyzing trends, gathering employer and learner insights, and supporting the development of evidence-based program concepts. The individual will work closely with country teams and global functions to analyze market opportunities, synthesize findings, and provide recommendations that inform program design and expansion decisions. The role will contribute to business case development and support the successful transition of new program concepts from research to implementation.

This is a regional role, initially focused on Colombia, with potential to expand across Latin America.

What will you do:

1. Market Research & Program Opportunity Identification

  • Conduct labor market research, including industry growth trends, hiring demand, and role-level analysis, to identify potential program opportunities.
  • Analyze employment trends, salary benchmarks, AI resilience, implementation considerations, and career pathways to support opportunity assessment.
  • Synthesize research findings into clear insights and recommendations for country and regional teams.
  • Support the use of existing program demand diagnostic methodologies and labor market intelligence tools (e.g., AI Job Market Agent, TalentNeuron, LinkedIn Talent Insights) to inform opportunity identification and assessment.
  • Prepare research summaries, market scans, and presentations to support program development discussions and decision-making.

2. Employer Insights & Demand Validation

  • Support employer outreach and engagement activities to gather insights on hiring demand, talent needs, and role requirements.
  • Conduct employer interviews, surveys, and desk research to identify workforce trends and employer pain points.
  • Synthesize employer feedback and translate findings into recommendations for program design and prioritization.
  • Support the maintenance of employer engagement records in Generation systems (e.g., Salesforce), including meeting notes, employer feedback, and demand signals.

3. Activity Mapping & Program Design Input

  • Support activity mapping and role analysis exercises in partnership with Curriculum & Instruction and other cross-functional teams.
  • Contribute insights on role scope, skills, competencies, and learner outcomes to inform program design decisions.
  • Synthesize activity findings and contribute to defining role scope, skills, and competencies required for successful employment.

4. Business Case Development & Stakeholder Support

  • Conduct learner research to identify target learner profiles, motivations, barriers, and program interest through methods such as focus groups and interviews.
  • Support the development of evidence-based business cases by gathering, analyzing, and synthesizing market, employer, learner, and operational data.
  • Develop reports, presentations, and briefing materials that communicate key findings and recommendations to internal stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with country and cross-functional teams to ensure business case assumptions and recommendations are grounded in evidence.
  • Prepare compelling materials to senior internal stakeholders to support decision-making, collect feedback and secure program approval

About you:

Experience:

  • 1-3 years of experience in research, consulting, strategy, business analysis, program development, or related fields
  • Experience conducting market research, data analysis, and developing insights to support strategic decision-making
  • Experience supporting business case development, program assessments, or growth initiatives
  • Exposure to employer engagement, talent market analysis, workforce development, education, or social impact programs is a plus
  • Experience working across multiple stakeholders and functions in a fast-paced environment preferred
  • Experience in Latin America or knowledge of regional labor market dynamics is desirable

Skills:

  • Strong analytical, research and structured problem-solving skills
  • Ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative data into clear insights and recommendations
  • Strong written communication and presentation skills, with attention to detail
  • Ability to develop reports, business case inputs, and decision-support materials
  • Effective project coordination and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Proactive, curious, and comfortable working with ambiguity and incomplete information
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional and multicultural teams
  • Proficiency in research and data analysis tools (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, labor market intelligence platforms, survey tools)
  • Fluent in English and Spanish (required); Portuguese desirable

Other:

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

At Torc, we have always believed that autonomous vehicle technology will transform how we travel, move freight, and do business.
A leader in autonomous driving since 2007, Torc has spent over a decade commercializing our solutions with experienced partners. Now a part of the Daimler family, we are focused solely on developing software for automated trucks to transform how the world moves freight.
Join us and catapult your career with the company that helped pioneer autonomous technology, and the first AV software company with the vision to partner directly with a truck manufacturer.

Meet the Team:
Accurate and highly available information about other actors and objects is fundamental to the safe operation of autonomous trucks. Core capabilities depend on accurate tracking estimates to ensure safe and efficient vehicle behavior.
The Tracking Team develops the ML models, state estimation algorithms, and production software responsible for associating and estimating the kinematics of other actors and objects in real time. Our solutions fuse information from multiple sensors and maintain robust performance despite sensor imperfections, environmental challenges, and system degradation. As part of this team, you will develop and deploy production-ready tracking solutions and help solve the challenges of bringing autonomous vehicle technology to real-world commercial applications.

You develop and deliver cybersecurity services that protect critical infrastructure, enable operational modernization, manage enterprise and operational risk, and support compliance with industry-specific regulatory requirements. This role demands deep expertise across IT and OT environments and the ability to guide CNR clients through complex business, technology, safety, and resilience challenges. You assess current and future cybersecurity capabilities, advise on leading practices, and shape cybersecurity strategies aligned with each client's business priorities, regulatory obligations, and operational realities.


The Work:


As a Cybersecurity Manager, you will manage complex information security engagements and workstreams. You will provide cybersecurity subject matter expertise, coordinate project delivery, and serve as a key point of contact for client security, business, and IT stakeholders, Accenture domain experts, and third-party teams. You will lead; manage plans, risks, budgets, and deliverables; and help shape practical solutions that achieve committed client outcomes.


As a team member, you'll be part of a Chemicals & Natural Resources industry team focused on applying cybersecurity expertise across the CNR value chain — from upstream exploration and extraction, to refining, processing, and distribution, through to chemical manufacturing and end-product delivery. You'll work closely with our CNR industry leaders to innovate and shape secure, resilient solutions for operational technology modernization, supply chain security, and industrial process safety.


  • Client Engagement: Build trusted working relationships with chemical, oil & gas, mining, and agricultural client stakeholders, translating their cybersecurity, safety, regulatory, and operational resilience priorities into actionable workplans and deliverables.
  • Initiative Delivery: Manage cybersecurity workstreams and project teams delivering solutions across cyber defense, AI-enabled security, risk management, and compliance, aligned with client objectives, scope, schedule, budget, and quality expectations.
  • CNR Insight & Strategy Development: Apply deep knowledge of CNR operations, regulatory obligations, threat trends, and technology modernization to shape practical client strategies tailored to chemical, energy, and natural resource environments.
  • Innovative Strategy Formulation: Collaborate with CNR clients to create and implement forward-looking strategies that secure operational technology modernization, process control systems, supply chain digitization, cloud adoption, and IT/OT convergence while protecting worker safety, environmental compliance, and operational continuity.
  • Secure AI: Support CNR clients in the secure adoption of artificial intelligence and machine learning across industrial operations — including AI-driven process optimization, predictive maintenance, and autonomous systems — ensuring AI deployments are implemented with security, safety, and governance controls embedded from inception.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Supervise and coach project team members, assign work, review deliverables, and foster a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing delivery environment.
  • Communication & Reporting: Develop clear recommendations, status reports, and executive-ready materials; present findings and delivery progress to client and Accenture stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:


  • Collaborate with client stakeholders to align security initiatives with business objectives and regulatory requirements.
  • Manage cybersecurity assessments, strategy workstreams, and implementation activities across CNR enterprise and operational environments, including IT, OT/ICS, cloud, process control networks, distributed control systems (DCS), SCADA, historian systems, and manufacturing execution systems (MES), while supporting applicable requirements such as IEC 62443, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-82, EPA Risk Management Program, TSA Security Directives, CIRCIA, API 1164, and industry-specific HSE regulations.
  • Support senior leaders in advising CNR stakeholders on integrating cybersecurity risk management into operational resilience, capital programs, plant modernization, emergency preparedness, and sustainability initiatives.
  • Manage CNR cybersecurity transformation workstreams focused on secure IT/OT convergence, network segmentation, internal network security monitoring, threat detection modernization, cyber resilience, and identity and access management for critical industrial infrastructure.
  • Facilitate CNR-specific threat modeling, incident response, and recovery-readiness activities for risks such as ransomware, nation-state activity, supply chain compromise, insecure remote access, and attacks affecting chemical plants, refineries, pipelines, or mining operations.
  • Work with architects, ecosystem partners, and technology vendors to develop scalable cybersecurity solutions that enable secure OT modernization, automation, cloud adoption, connected field devices, and digital supply chain services without compromising operational safety or continuity.
  • Contribute CNR cybersecurity expertise to client engagements, proposals, and internal forums.
  • Support Accenture Security and CNR teams in developing differentiated offerings, reusable assets, and go-to-market materials for CNR clients.
  • Establishing trusted relationships with our clients

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Here's what you need

  • Minimum of 6 years of experience designing, developing, implementing, or managing solutions across cybersecurity domains such as industry strategy, security operations, risk management, digital identity, network security, vulnerability management, data protection, cloud security, and OT security.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience leading project teams or workstreams, including planning, delivery management, risk and issue management, and quality review.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience delivering cybersecurity solutions for chemical manufacturers, oil & gas operators, mining companies, or agricultural enterprises across enterprise IT or operational technology environments.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience

Bonus points if you have

  • Certifications such as CISM, CISSP, CRISC, TOGAF, SABSA are highly preferred.
  • Experience with CNR industry cybersecurity and regulatory frameworks, including IEC 62443, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-82, EPA RMP Cybersecurity, TSA Security Directives, CIRCIA, API 1164, and relevant HSE/process safety regulations is highly preferred.

Employee type: Full time, Permanent

Location: Ontario - Remote
